summary: Wilde's society comedy of political corruption and blackmail, contrasting public and private morality, with the dandy Lord Goring as raisonneur and a buried secret threatening a statesman's career.

title: AN INVOCATION
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A spell-song from the play Remorse invoking a spirit, with chapel masses, a tolling knell and a moonlit sea. Themes: the supernatural, death, religion.

title: AN INVOCATION
author: Coleridge
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: A brief lyric invoking the Muse as the companion and soother of the poet's hours, sent to win praise and bring back joy.

title: AN ODE IN THE MANNER OF ANACREON
author: Coleridge
summary: A short Anacreontic lyric in which the speaker catches Love among roses, drinks him in his cup, and feels the captive god fluttering within his breast.

title: AN ODE TO THE RAIN
author: Coleridge
summary: Half-comic ode begging the rain to depart so three reunited friends may be alone. Themes of friendship, weather, and gentle satire in mock-ode form.

title: An Old Man’s Thought of School
author: Whitman
cluster: The Journey · The Quest · The Pilgrim
summary: Occasional poem for a school inauguration; sees children as immortal ships launching on the soul's voyage and links education to America's future.

title: Animula
author: Eliot
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: The simple soul issuing from God, growing fearful and selfish in time; childhood, the burden of experience, the viaticum and prayer for the dead.

title: ANNA AND HARLAND
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A melancholy sonnet-ballad telling of lovers killed in a duel with the woman's brother, her grief-driven death, and her lingering ghost, framed by the speaker's reverie of memory at her tomb.

title: Annabel Lee
author: Poe
summary: A musical ballad lamenting the death of a beautiful young beloved in a kingdom by the sea, whose love outlasts death; centers on love, grief, the death of a beautiful woman, and undying devotion.

title: ANOTHER VERSION.
author: Coleridge
summary: An alternate version of the grave-and-Cherub-Hope quatrain (on the death of 'Perdita') with scholarly notes on the Heraclitus Sibyl fragment; mortality, hope and textual commentary.

title: ANSWER TO A CHILD’S QUESTION
author: Coleridge
summary: Light lyric song imagining the birds declaring 'I love and I love', joining love, spring and birdsong. A children's nature-song.

title: ANTHEM FOR THE CHILDREN OF CHRIST’S HOSPITAL
author: Coleridge
summary: A devotional hymn of gratitude invoking seraphs and divine compassion, celebrating charity that relieves the poor and orphaned children of Christ's Hospital.

title: anti religious thought
author: Chesterton
summary: Historical essay on the rise and short-lived 'Age of Reason' rationalism between the Reformation and the Romantic movement (Voltaire, Montaigne, Rousseau). Themes: faith and doubt, history of ideas, the Reformation and rationalism.

title: anti-puritan
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: A ballade with refrain ('Will someone take me to a pub?') mocking earnest Progressive reformers and celebrating fellowship, beer and the common man. Themes: satire of society, the common man, anti-puritanism, fellowship.

title: ANTONY AND CLEOPATRA
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Shakespeare's Roman tragedy in blank verse dramatizing the ruinous passion of Mark Antony and the Egyptian queen Cleopatra, set against the disintegrating triumvirate; its themes are love as empire-destroying desire, the conflict of Rome and Egypt, and transcendent death.

title: Apollo and the Graces
author: Keats
summary: A short song set to a Mozart air in which Apollo invites the three Graces to ride with him across autumn's golden fields; a light mythological lyric of music, sun and joy.

title: APOLOGETIC PREFACE TO ‘FIRE, FAMINE, AND SLAUGHTER’
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A critical-apologetic prose essay defending his War-Eclogue against the charge of malignity, distinguishing poetic imagination from real cruelty, with a long defence of Milton and Jeremy Taylor and the Church's toleration.

title: APOLOGIA PRO VITA SUA
author: Coleridge
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: An epigram on the poet's imagination, whose 'gifted ken' sees phantoms of sublimity in coals and pipe-smoke, a miniature ars poetica of the shaping imagination.

title: APPENDIX POEMS WRITTEN IN EARLY YOUTH
author: Eliot
summary: Appendix gathering Eliot's juvenilia (A Fable for Feasters, carpe-diem lyrics, school odes, Laforgue-influenced poems); ranges from mock-heroic comic narrative to wistful lyrics on time, love and mutability.

title: ApprAndCritOfChDickens
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Chesterton's 1911 book of critical introductions to each of Dickens's novels, championing his exuberant characters, his defence of the common man, and the social vision of his fiction. Form: literary criticism; themes: the common man, social injustice, the artist and society.

title: aquinas
author: Chesterton
summary: Chesterton's popular biography and apologetic study of St. Thomas Aquinas, presenting Thomism as a philosophy that affirms Creation, reconciles faith and reason through the Aristotelian revolution, and stands against both Manichee pessimism and the later Augustinian-Lutheran revolt.

title: Are You the New Person Drawn Toward Me?
author: Whitman
summary: Interrogative warning to a would-be lover that the poet is not the ideal imagined; identity, illusion (maya), and the uncertainty of love and friendship.

title: ARGUMENT
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: The prose Argument plus text of the Ode to the Departing Year, summarising its vision of divine Providence, war, and the prophesied downfall of the country.

title: ARGUMENT.
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: The stanza-by-stanza Argument to 'France: An Ode' explaining its movement from devotion to liberty through revolutionary hope and recantation to liberty rooted in God and Nature; paratext on freedom and disillusionment.

title: ARIEL POEMS
author: Eliot
summary: Section header that contains Journey of the Magi: a Christian quest/pilgrimage poem on the Nativity, winter journey, birth and death.

title: aristocrat
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: A ballad-like lyric in which the Devil is figured as a charming gentleman whose golden house breeds endless ennui and damnation; a satirical-theological warning about pleasure, pride and the emptiness of worldly luxury.

title: arthur
author: Chesterton
summary: A sonnet mocking the over-skeptical scholar who would explain away King Arthur; it defends legend and the imaginative truth of the Arthurian tradition against reductive rationalism.

title: artist
author: Chesterton
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A comic narrative poem satirizing the aesthete and the cult of art-for-art's-sake, ending with a dream where Art unmakes the order of nature; defends childlike wonder and the simple love of created things.

title: As Adam Early in the Morning
author: Whitman
summary: Closing Children of Adam lyric: the speaker as Adam at dawn inviting touch of his unashamed body; the body, innocence, dawn, Eden.

title: As at Thy Portals Also Death
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse elegy and verbal tombstone to the poet's dead mother as the ideal woman; themes of death, grief, motherhood and memory.

title: As Consequent, Etc.
author: Whitman
summary: Prefatory poem of Autumn Rivulets figuring the poet's songs as autumn streams flowing to the mystic ocean of time and death; rivers, sea, shells, and continuity of life.

title: As I Ebb’d with the Ocean of Life
author: Whitman
summary: Walking the shore in autumn the poet despairs, feeling himself mere drift and debris, calling the sea his father; free-verse crisis-lyric on doubt, the self, mortality and nature.

title: As I Lay with My Head in Your Lap Camerado
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: A confessional address to a comrade: the poet's restless dangerous words unsettle settled laws, urging onward without knowing the destination; comradeship, rebellion and uncertain quest.

title: As I Ponder’d in Silence
author: Whitman
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: A phantom of old poets demands the theme of war; Whitman answers that his book too sings a greater war for body and soul. Free-verse poetic-vocation lyric.

title: As I Sit Writing Here
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse lyric fearing that the aches and ennui of old age filter into his songs; themes of old age, writing and melancholy.

title: As I Walk These Broad Majestic Days
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse lyric set in postwar days of peace asserting the poet's spiritual realities above science and industry; themes of democracy, war's aftermath and the soul.

title: As I Was Saying
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A collection of witty, paradoxical essays on modern life (Puritanism, Voltaire, Darwinism, education, Totalitarianism, change and impermanence), satirizing fashionable progress and defending tradition, common sense and the permanent things.

title: As I Watch the Ploughman Ploughing
author: Whitman
summary: Quatrain reading agricultural labor as an analogy for mortality: life is the tillage and death the harvest according.

title: As If a Phantom Caress’d Me
author: Whitman
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Brief shore lyric in which a loved phantom that caressed the speaker vanishes in glimmering light, leaving only hateful mocking presences.

title: As the Greek’s Signal Flame
author: Whitman
summary: Like an ancient Greek beacon hailing a hero, the poet lifts a kindled brand from Manhattan's shore to an Old Poet.

title: As the Time Draws Nigh
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse lyric anticipating the poet's death and the silencing of his song; themes of mortality, the book and the soul.

title: As They Draw to a Close
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse valedictory summing the aims of his songs and accepting death as the equal of life; themes of the soul, death and the book.

title: As Toilsome I Wander’d Virginia’s Woods
author: Whitman
summary: In autumn woods the speaker finds an unknown soldier's grave with a scrawled epitaph that haunts him for years; an elegy of remembrance and comradeship.

title: AS YOU LIKE IT
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A pastoral romantic comedy in which exiles flee a usurping court to the Forest of Arden, where Rosalind, disguised as a youth, tutors Orlando in love; it celebrates the green world, disguise, and the contrast of court and country, voicing the Seven Ages of Man.

title: ascetic
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: A satirical ballad contrasting a full-blooded pagan's joy in wine, love and war with the joyless, life-denying modern 'Heathen' Higgins; defends faith-grounded delight against a sterile secular asceticism.

title: ASH-WEDNESDAY 1930
author: Eliot
summary: Opening of Eliot's first overtly Christian sequence ('Because I do not hope to turn again'); renunciation, penitence, the will to faith and the prayer to learn to care and not to care.

title: Ashes of Soldiers
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: A free-verse elegy summoning the phantom dead of both armies and vowing undying love to fertilize the earth; themes of war's cost, death, comradeship and immortality.

title: asparagus
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: A whimsical paradoxical essay using asparagus etiquette to satirize aristocracy, social distinction and the cult of fashionable 'Progress' as artificial passwords.

title: ASSOCIATION OF IDEAS
author: Coleridge
summary: Three epigrams illustrating associative principles (likeness, contrast, time), the last linking the poet's fall on a slide to Napoleon's Moscow disaster; comic verse on memory, association, and historical reference.

title: Assurances
author: Whitman
summary: Litany of 'I do not doubt' affirmations of cosmic order, the limitless soul, and that Heavenly Death provides for all; serene faith against doubt.

title: (At Graduation 1905)
author: Eliot
summary: A schoolboy graduation ode in fourteen sestets: pupils as colonists setting sail into the unknown future, valedictory on memory, time, progress and farewell to the school.

title: Aunt Helen
author: Eliot
summary: Ironic epitaph-portrait of a respectable spinster aunt whose death loosens the servants' decorum; satire of genteel society, mortality and the emptiness of convention.

title: AUTHORS AND PUBLISHERS
author: Coleridge
summary: An epigram glossing Pope's line on wits, joking that nowadays every wit hangs by a bookseller; satire of the literary marketplace.

title: ball and cross
author: Chesterton
summary: A philosophical adventure novel in which a devout Catholic Highlander (MacIan) and an atheist (Turnbull) try to fight a duel over God's existence while a sceptical, indifferent modern society and the Satanic Professor Lucifer conspire to stop them, ending in an apocalyptic asylum fire; dramatizes faith vs doubt, good vs evil and the modern flight from belief.

title: Ballad Of Abbreviations
author: Chesterton
summary: A comic satirical ballad mocking the American cult of speed, hustle and verbal shortcuts as a symbol of misguided modern 'Progress'.

title: Ballad of St Barbara
author: Chesterton
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: A narrative ballad set at the WWI Battle of the Marne, interweaving the martyrdom of St Barbara (patron of gunners) with the defence of Paris; a meditation on faith, martyrdom, liberty against tyranny, and sudden death in war.

title: BalladStBarbara
author: Chesterton
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: Chesterton's 1922 verse collection containing the title ballad and other poems on the Great War, the Crusades (Horns of Hattin), distributist social critique, nostalgia and the lost faith of the modern world.

title: Barnaby Rudge
author: Dickens
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Dickens's historical novel set around the 1780 anti-Catholic Gordon ('No Popery') Riots in London, weaving a murder mystery and a love plot through scenes of mob violence and sectarian fanaticism. Central themes: mob violence and order vs chaos, religious bigotry and fanaticism, social injustice, and the destructive cost of riot, with the innocent Barnaby and his raven at its heart.

title: BARON GUELPH OF ADELSTAN. A FRAGMENT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A narrative ballad fragment of a courtier-baron who forsakes court pomp for shepherd's crook and the village dance; pastoral retreat from courtly life.

title: Beat! Beat! Drums!
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: A pounding incantatory war-song in which drums and bugles shatter church, school, marriage and ordinary life; war's intrusion on the peaceful world.

title: Before Morning
author: Eliot
summary: Dawn lyric of fresh and withered flowers turning toward the light; fragrance of bloom and decay together — a vanitas/transience image at daybreak.

title: Beginners
author: Whitman
summary: Meditation on great original souls who appear at intervals, dear and dreadful, fated and misvalued; the prophet/outcast and the price of greatness.

title: Beginning My Studies
author: Whitman
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: Ecstatic wonder at the first step of consciousness, sense and motion; joy, wonder and gratitude, the sublime in the ordinary. Short free-verse lyric.

title: Behold This Swarthy Face
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Self-portrait of the unadorned poet kissed by a Manhattanese comrade; the 'salute of American comrades land and sea'; comradeship, the body, the common man.

title: BEN JONSON: A NYMPH’S PASSION
author: Coleridge
summary: Jonson's love-lyric with Coleridge's modernized version 'Mutual Passion': a speaker hides her beloved's name for fear of rivals; concealed mutual love, jealousy and the praise of a fair youth.

title: Ben Nevis - a Dialogue
author: Keats
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: A comic verse dialogue in which Mrs Cameron flirts with the personified, waking mountain Ben Nevis, who lusts grotesquely after her. It is a burlesque mixing the sublime mountain, the supernatural, and absurd desire.

title: Berenice
author: Poe
summary: A gothic horror tale in which the monomaniac Egaeus, obsessed with his dying cousin Berenice's teeth, violates her premature grave to extract them; explores madness, obsession, decay, and the horror of the body.

title: Bivouac on a Mountain Side
author: Whitman
summary: An imagistic night-camp scene: a halting army, scattered camp-fires, shadowy men and horses, and over all the eternal stars; war set against cosmic permanence.

title: Bleak House
author: Dickens
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Dickens's great London novel built around the interminable Chancery suit Jarndyce and Jarndyce, opening in fog as an emblem of legal obfuscation; it interlaces Esther Summerson's first-person narrative with an omniscient satire of law, philanthropy, and aristocracy, and embeds a detective plot (Inspector Bucket) around Lady Dedlock's secret. Central themes: social injustice and the law, the city and fog, secrecy and detection, class and reform.

title: Bon-Bon
author: Poe
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: A comic tale in which a vain restaurateur-philosopher is visited by the Devil, who eats souls and declines to buy Bon-Bon's; a satire on metaphysics, wine, and the philosopher's pride through a Faustian comedy.

title: Bravo, Paris Exposition!
author: Whitman
summary: An occasional greeting wafting America's love and good-will across the sea to the Paris Exposition, celebrating fraternity among nations and inherited debts to forebears.

title: Bright star! would I were steadfast as thou art
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet longing for the steadfastness of a star, but redirected to eternal repose on the beloved's breast; love, constancy, mortality and the wish to live forever or swoon to death.

title: Broad Minded Bishop
author: Chesterton
summary: A four-line satirical epigram mocking modern 'broad-minded' sensibility at the expense of St Francis's holy charity.

title: Broadway
author: Whitman
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: The crowded New York street as a teeming theatre of human passions, an unspeakable show and lesson of life.

title: Burbank with a Baedeker: Bleistein with a Cigar
author: Eliot
summary: Quatrain satire set in a decayed Venice of tourists and money; the ruin of culture, time's decline, money and a vein of antisemitic caricature; vanitas amid the city of ruins.

title: BURKE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: A sonnet in which a personified Freedom mourns Burke's apostasy from the cause of liberty; themes of genius corrupted, political betrayal, and lost ideals.

title: Burnt Norton 1935
author: Eliot
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: First Quartet: time present/past/future, the rose-garden, the still point of the turning world, drained pool and light; memory, time, faith, the quest.

title: Bustopher Jones: the Cat About Town
author: Eliot
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: Comic verse on the fat, fastidious St James's club cat who feasts his way around London's clubs; light satire of the man-about-town.

title: By Blue Ontario’s Shore
author: Whitman
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: Long programmatic ode in which a phantom commands the poet to chant the throes of Democracy; a manifesto of the American bard, the self, the nation, and the cost of the secession war.

title: By Broad Potomac’s Shore
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse lyric invoking Virginia's spring, blood-red roses and deathless grass to perfume the poet's book; themes of nature, spring and the immortality of verse.

title: By the Bivouac’s Fitful Flame
author: Whitman
summary: By a flickering camp-fire the speaker's thoughts wind in solemn procession over life and death, home and the absent loved; a meditative night-camp lyric.

title: cabman
author: Chesterton
summary: A 'tremendous trifle' essay-parable in which an honest but mistaken cabman becomes the occasion for reflecting on certainty, scepticism and the defence of common-sense reality against philosophical doubt.

title: CALIDORE
author: Keats
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Spenserian narrative fragment following the knight Calidore through a lush idealized landscape; chivalric romance steeped in nature-description and medieval pageantry.

title: Camps of Green
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: A free-verse lyric extending the soldiers' bivouac into the universal camp of the dead beneath the grass; themes of death, war, sleep and comradeship.

title: CARDENIO - A BRIEF ACCOUNT
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: An editorial prose account of the lost play Cardenio, attributed to Shakespeare and Fletcher and based on a Don Quixote episode; it summarizes a tragicomedy of rape, betrayed friendship, a disguised wronged heroine, madness for revenge, repentance and reconciliation.

title: carol
author: Chesterton
summary: A tender devotional lyric on the Christ-child in Mary's arms, contrasting the weary world with the divine peace of the Nativity.

title: Cat Morgan Introduces Himself
author: Eliot
cluster: The Outsider · Fall from Innocence · The (Reputed) Fallen Woman
summary: Comic dramatic monologue in cockney by a retired pirate cat now keeping a Bloomsbury door; light verse with a sea-rover persona.

title: CATULLIAN HENDECASYLLABLES
author: Coleridge
summary: A classicizing erotic idyll set on a 'Milesian' island temple, in which a praying priestess and a moonlit sea-voyage end in sensual union, framed in Catullan metre.

title: Cavalry Crossing a Ford
author: Whitman
cluster: Swords and Weapons · The Battlefield · Horse
summary: An imagistic miniature of a cavalry line snaking across a silvery river, arms flashing and guidon flags fluttering; a painterly battlefield scene.

title: chalk
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: An essay in which a walk on the Sussex downs to draw with chalk becomes a meditation on wonder, the positive nature of virtue ('white is a color'), and the sacramental quality of created England.

title: Chanting the Square Deific
author: Whitman
summary: Four-sided godhead chant voicing in turn the stern Father (Jehovah/Brahm/Saturn), the Christ-consolator, defiant Satan, and the all-pervading Santa Spirita soul.

title: CharlesDickens
author: Chesterton
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Chesterton's critical biography of Charles Dickens, celebrating his greatness, his common humanity, his comedy and his social conscience while placing him in Victorian England and the radical tradition.

title: cheese
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A whimsical essay using the 'neglect of cheese' in poetry to praise local, varied, living tradition over uniform mechanized modern civilization; defends rootedness and the sacramental joy of common food.

title: child psychology
author: Chesterton
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: An essay defending genuine nursery-rhyme nonsense and childlike imagination against modern 'child-psychology', satirizing experts (Freud, Wells) who put nonsense in the wrong place.

title: childsnow
author: Chesterton
summary: A mystical Nativity lyric: the Christ-child born at the inn at the world's end while the old pagan gods die; a hymn of the heart of the earth as a star.

title: CHOLERA CURED BEFORE-HAND
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: A comic-grotesque doggerel 'premonition' advising the poor against drink and dirt to avoid the cholera-devil, with political jabs at Cobbett and O'Connell; the grotesque, disease, and social satire of the poor.

title: CHORUSES FROM ‘THE ROCK’ 1934
author: Eliot
summary: Choric pageant verse defending the Church and church-building against secular modernity; faith, the Word, the timekept City, light, anti-industrialism.

title: CHRISTABEL
author: Coleridge
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: An unfinished Gothic-medieval verse romance in which the innocent Christabel shelters the uncanny Geraldine, who exerts a sinister enchantment; themes of innocence, temptation, the supernatural and the uncanny.

title: CHRISTIAN RELIGION
author: Coleridge
summary: Variorum notes and verse-fragments to 'Religious Musings' on the Nativity vision, the despised Galilaean, the apocalyptic fall of Babylon and union of religion with power; themes of faith, apocalypse, original sin, and critique of established churches.

title: Christianity and Rationalism
author: Chesterton
summary: An apologetic essay defending Christian faith and reason against the rationalist critique, arguing for the reasonableness of belief and the limits of pure rationalism.

title: christmas-games
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A playful essay imagining that children's games preceded practical objects, used to celebrate the ritual mystery behind everyday things, the wisdom of the peasantry, and to satirize gloomy modern science (Freud, Wells).

title: christmas-poem
author: Chesterton
summary: A Nativity lyric on the homeless holy family in the stable as the true home of all men; contrasts the wandering exile of the human heart with the divine homecoming of Christmas.

title: CHRISTOPHER HARVEY THE SYNAGOGUE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: Devotional poem on Christmas Day with Coleridge's substituted lines, addressing the sun and the birth of Christ as a 'primal great lucific light' that gives sight to souls; Nativity hymn on light and incarnation.

title: CHRIST’S HOSPITAL
author: Coleridge
summary: A comic burlesque ode versifying Euclid's first proposition, turning a geometric demonstration into mock-Pindaric verse with political asides on the balance of power.

title: Circe’s Palace
author: Eliot
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: Mythological lyric set in Circe's enchanted, sinister garden of fanged flowers, panthers and a python, where beasts have the eyes of men once known; menace, enchantment and degradation.

title: City of Orgies
author: Whitman
summary: Manhattan poem declaring it is not the city's spectacles but the flashing eyes of lovers offering love that repay the poet; the city, eyes, love and desire.

title: City of Ships
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: An apostrophe to warlike Manhattan, city of ships and tides, whose song is now red war; an urban patriotic war-chant.

title: cockneys
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A humorous essay defending London Cockney humour and the comic genius of the city's poor (Chaucer, Dickens, Lamb, Johnson), praising laughter that masks sorrow and the dignity of the common Londoner.

title: COLLECTED POEMS 1909–1962
author: Eliot
summary: Title/dedication page of Eliot's collected verse, opening with the Prufrock dedication to Jean Verdenal (mort aux Dardanelles) and a Dante epigraph; frames the volume's preoccupation with mortality, memory and the elegiac.

title: COLOGNE
author: Coleridge
summary: A comic epigram on the filthy stench-ridden town of Cologne, asking what divine power shall now wash the Rhine. Themes: satire, the city, comic grotesque.

title: Come Up from the Fields Father
author: Whitman
summary: An elegiac narrative: a letter from the front announces the only son's death amid an autumnal Ohio farm; the grief of the bereaved mother. War's cost on the home front.

title: Common Man
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A posthumous collection of essays whose title piece argues that modern emancipation has actually persecuted the common man and common sense; ranges over literary criticism (Dickens, Tolstoi, Henry James, Browning), faith, philosophy and democracy.

title: COMPARATIVE BREVITY OF GREEK AND ENGLISH
author: Coleridge
summary: A two-line English rendering of a Greek epigram about a man who hangs himself with a rope left by one who found lost gold; a jeu d'esprit on translation, brevity, and money.

title: Complete Prose Works: Specimen Days and Collect, November Boughs and Goodbye My Fancy
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: Whitman's collected prose: autobiographical Specimen Days, Civil War hospital memoranda, nature notes, and literary essays celebrating democracy, the common people, and nature.

title: COMPOSED WHILE CLIMBING THE LEFT ASCENT OF BROCKLEY COOMB,
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: A descriptive nature-sonnet on a Somersetshire hill-climb and the landscape's luxury, longing for the absent beloved; themes of nature, the sublime, and love.

title: Compulsory Education
author: Chesterton
summary: Essay on the Scopes 'Monkey Trial' arguing that compulsory secular education is a new act of conformity that lets professors preach materialist creeds; defends the Tennessee Fundamentalists on grounds of justice.

title: CONSTANCY TO AN IDEAL OBJECT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A meditation on the yearning thought, the one constant in a world of change, ending with the Brocken-spectre image of a rustic worshipping his own projected shadow. Themes: imagination, unrequited/ideal love, illusion, home and exile.

title: Continuities
author: Whitman
summary: Nothing is ever truly lost; body, sun and frozen clods all return with spring, an affirmation of immortality and eternal renewal.

title: Conversation Galante
author: Eliot
summary: Ironic flirtation lyric: the speaker's moonlit posturing deflated by the lady's cool questions; love as failed communication, irony and self-deflating wit.

title: conversion
author: Chesterton
summary: Apologetic treatise on the psychology and stages of conversion to Catholicism, treating the convert as a modern witness/martyr to the truth of the Faith.

title: convert
author: Chesterton
summary: Sonnet on the poet's conversion: the world turns over, the sages' maps become 'less than dust' because 'my name is Lazarus and I live' — faith as resurrection and rebirth.

title: Coriolan
author: Eliot
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Two-part dramatic fragment on the Roman hero-statesman: triumphal march, militarist spectacle, hollow bureaucracy; dust, the still point, power and emptiness.

title: CORIOLANUS
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Shakespeare's last Roman tragedy in austere blank verse, on the proud warrior Caius Marcius Coriolanus whose contempt for the plebeians brings banishment and his vengeful alliance with Rome's enemies; themes are pride, class conflict, honour, and the politics of the state.

title: Cousin Nancy
author: Eliot
summary: Satiric New England portrait of a modern emancipated young woman watched over by Matthew Arnold and Emerson, 'guardians of the faith'; satire of society and the decay of tradition.

title: Crossing Brooklyn Ferry
author: Whitman
summary: Meditation across time uniting the poet with future ferry-crossers; the city, the river/sea, the crowd, time and the bond between self and future others.

title: CYMBELINE
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A late tragicomic romance set in legendary Roman-era Britain, weaving a wager on Innogen's chastity, banishment, disguise, a wicked queen, and the descent of Jupiter into a web of miraculous reunions and reconciliations; themes are fidelity, jealousy, providence and restoration.

title: Daisy’s Song
author: Keats
summary: A light lyric song voiced by a daisy delighting in the spring, the sun and moon, and watching the world unseen. Its motifs are spring, flowers, the sun and moon, and joy in nature.

title: Dans le Restaurant
author: Eliot
summary: French poem of a decrepit waiter's childhood erotic memory and the speaker's disgust, closing with the drowned Phlebas the Phoenician; lust, the grotesque, memory and death by water.

title: Darest Thou Now O Soul
author: Whitman
cluster: The Journey · The Quest · The Pilgrim
summary: Lyric address summoning the soul to walk into the unknown region beyond death, where only Time and Space remain and the self bursts forth fulfilled.

title: David Copperfield
author: Dickens
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Dickens's most autobiographical novel, a first-person bildungsroman following an orphaned boy from neglected childhood through hardship, schooling and apprenticeship to maturity as a writer; central themes of memory, the disciplined heart, social injustice and the growth of identity.

title: De Profundis
author: Wilde
cluster: Martyrdom · The Martyr / Saint · The Cross
summary: Long prison letter charting Wilde's spiritual development through sorrow, humility and conversion, with Christ reimagined as the supreme individualist and romantic artist.

title: DE PROFUNDIS CLAMAVI
author: Coleridge
summary: Fragments of weary longing for death (adapted from a Scots ballad), a tropic-tree idol image, love, soul-and-body reflection and birdsong; despair set against tenderness.

title: DEAR BROTHER JEM
author: Coleridge
summary: A literary-satirical epigram mocking a prolific but forgettable versifier who writes faster than printers can set.

title: Death of General Grant
author: Whitman
summary: Elegy for General Grant, a hero withdrawing from history's stage of war and peace alongside Lincoln and Lee.

title: debate
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Transcribed public debate (Belloc in the chair) between Chesterton and Shaw on property, socialism vs distributism: Shaw would distribute wealth, Chesterton would distribute power and ownership.

title: Defence of the Islands
author: Eliot
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: WWII occasional piece written after Dunkirk, memorializing British war effort by land, sea and air; patriotic elegy for the war dead.

title: DEJECTION: AN ODE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: Major Romantic ode lamenting the loss of joy and the failure of the imaginative shaping spirit; nature lives only as the soul gives. Storm, Aeolian lute, and inward fountains figure spiritual desolation.

title: Delicate Cluster
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: Drum-Taps apostrophe to the American flag as 'flag of life' and 'flag of death,' fusing battle, patriotism, and a maternal sacred emblem.

title: deluge
author: Chesterton
summary: Ballad-like lyric of a lone tattered man standing up amid the biblical flood to drink defiantly to God — gratitude, defiance and faith against cosmic catastrophe.

title: democracy
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Essay defending the democratic ideal against the inhuman, indirect machinery of industrial capitalism, blaming original sin rather than the people for political evils.

title: DES KNABEN WUNDERHORN
author: Coleridge
summary: German folk-song ('Wenn ich ein Vöglein wär'): the lover wishes to be a bird to fly to the beloved, is with her only in dream, and wakes alone; a folk lyric of longing, separation and dreams.

title: DESTRUCTION OF THE BASTILE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: An exuberant Pindaric ode celebrating the fall of the Bastille and the triumph of Liberty over tyranny, hoping freedom will spread to every land.

title: DEVONSHIRE ROADS
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Road · Napoleonic Wars / the Navy
summary: A mock-furious ode cursing a muddy Devonshire road, comparing it to Milton's hellish paths and heaping imprecations upon the bog.

title: diabolist
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: Autobiographical essay recounting a terrifying art-school conversation with a devil-worshipper, dramatising the moment Chesterton became orthodox and the abyss between good and evil.

title: dickens Britannica
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Biographical-critical appreciation of Charles Dickens written for the Encyclopaedia Britannica, praising his comic, superhuman imagination and his roots in the insecure Victorian middle class.

title: Diddling
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A mock-scientific satirical essay defining man as 'an animal that diddles' and cataloguing petty swindles; a comic anatomy of deception, the trickster, and social satire.

title: Dirge for Two Veterans
author: Whitman
summary: A formal dirge for a father and son fallen together, buried in a double grave under a phantom moon to the music of drums and bugles; grief, mourning and the dead-march.

title: divorce
author: Chesterton
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Book-length polemic defending the permanence of the marriage vow as the foundation of the free family and a bulwark against slavery, attacking divorce as a plutocratic superstition.

title: Divorce Democracy
author: Chesterton
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Pamphlet arguing that extending divorce is the rich man's weapon against the poor family, defending marriage as a democratic vow of 'for better, for worse'.

title: dogs
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Familiar essay on the ancient bond between man and dog by the fireside, using the relationship to mock reductive evolutionary biology and affirm the antiquity of human nature.

title: DOMESTIC PEACE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Song from 'The Fall of Robespierre' asking where domestic peace is found: in a cottaged vale far from pomp and rebellion; peace, virtue, home, memory.

title: Don Quixote
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: Satirical novel and 'parable for social reformers' in which a librarian reenacts the Middle Ages and becomes a quixotic knight-errant, blending medievalist romance, distributist politics, and conversion.

title: donkey
author: Chesterton
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: Lyric in which the despised, grotesque donkey keeps its secret: it too had 'one far fierce hour' when palms were strewn before it on Palm Sunday — the lowly exalted through Christ.

title: DONNE: ECLOGUE. ‘ON UNWORTHY WISDOM
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Donne's lines (altered by Coleridge for The Friend) on the recluse hermit knowing heaven's glory, with man as an epitome of God's book of creatures.

title: Doubts About Darwinism
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Essay marshalling common-sense objections to natural selection, arguing Darwinism has become a defensive dogma appealing to authority rather than explanation.

title: Dream-Land
author: Poe
cluster: The Journey · The Quest · The Pilgrim
summary: A visionary lyric describing a journey to a weird, melancholy realm ruled by an Eidolon named Night, out of Space and Time; explores dream, death, memory, and a haunted otherworld of grief.

title: Dreams
author: Poe
summary: Youthful lyric exalting dream-life over waking reality, mingling melancholy, imagination, and a longing for an eternal visionary state.

title: DRINKING VERSUS THINKING
author: Coleridge
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: A drinking song against the 'new philosophy', urging merry men to live while able and shove dull philosophy dead-drunk beneath the table; carpe diem, wine, and satire of abstract reasoning.

title: Drum-Taps
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: Whitman's Civil War poem cluster of free-verse lyrics: drums and marches, soldiers and comrades, the wound-dresser and hospital vigils, grief for the dead, and reconciliation. Sampling confirms central concerns with the cost of war, patriotism, loss, heroism, blood and death on the battlefield.

title: DURA NAVIS
author: Coleridge
summary: A schoolboy poem warning a venturous youth against going to sea, cataloguing storm, naval battle, famine, and cannibalism, and praising the contented peace of home and domestic love.

title: DUTY SURVIVING SELF-LOVE THE ONLY SURE FRIEND OF DECLINING LIFE
author: Coleridge
summary: A soliloquy counselling that one shine on with love and duty even as old friends grow dim and unchanged self meets a changed world. Themes: ageing, duty, friendship, transience.

title: Earth, My Likeness
author: Whitman
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: Poet sees in the impassive earth a hidden fierce force mirroring the inexpressible passion roused by an athlete-lover; nature, desire, the body and the inexpressible.

title: East Coker 1940
author: Eliot
summary: Second Quartet: 'In my beginning is my end', houses rise and fall, rustic dancers long under earth, humility and the dark; mutability, faith, eternal return.

title: EASTER HOLIDAYS
author: Coleridge
summary: An early lyric ode (1787) celebrating Easter, spring, and youthful joy, then turning to the inevitability of future woe and the consolation of steadfast virtue.

title: EDWARD III
author: Shakespeare
summary: Collaborative history play on Edward III's wars against Scotland and France (Crecy, Calais) and his attempted seduction of the virtuous Countess of Salisbury. Central themes: kingship, war and conquest, honour, chastity vs lust, mercy.

title: Eidolons
author: Whitman
summary: Metaphysical chant on eidolons (ideal images) as the permanent reality behind mutable matter; identity, immortality, mutability, the prophet-bard. Incantatory free verse.

title: Eighteen Sixty-One
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: An apostrophe to the war-year 1861 personified as an armed, sunburnt soldier striding across the continent; a patriotic war-poem of national crisis.

title: Eldorado
author: Poe
cluster: The Journey · The Quest · The Pilgrim
summary: Ballad of a knight's lifelong quest for a golden land he never finds, ending with a pilgrim's counsel to ride down the Valley of the Shadow.

title: Election Day, November, 1884
author: Whitman
summary: Names America's peaceful quadrennial election, not its landscapes, as its mightiest scene; democracy as a swordless conflict.

title: elegy
author: Chesterton
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: Short ironic elegy: those who worked for England have home graves, those who fought lie afar, but those who rule 'have no graves as yet' — patriotic satire on the ruling class.

title: ELEGY IMITATED FROM ONE OF AKENSIDE’S BLANK-VERSE INSCRIPTIONS
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Graveyard elegy for Edmund, dead of ill-requited love, and the guilt-haunted Matilda; death, the grave, unrequited love, guilt and conscience.

title: Eleonora
author: Poe
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Prose tale of innocent love in a paradisal valley, a dying beloved's vow, and a haunted narrator absolved for a second love.

title: ELISA
author: Coleridge
summary: Imitations/translations of an epigram of Claudian turning a gift into frankincense and myrrh; a graceful compliment to a friend who sends gifts, in Latin and English.

title: Emma
author: Austen
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Austen's comic novel of manners about a clever, self-deceived young woman whose matchmaking schemes misfire; central themes are marriage, class, self-knowledge, and the gap between appearance and reality in a rural English community.

title: Endymion - A Poetic Romance
author: Keats
summary: A long mythological romance in heroic couplets following the shepherd-prince Endymion's quest for the moon-goddess Cynthia/Phoebe through earth, sea and underworld; beauty as eternal joy, visionary love and the spiritualization of the mortal lover.

title: ephemeral
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Preface to All Things Considered defending hasty journalism, attacking 'modernism' as snobbery and philanthropy as covert religious persecution.

title: EPIGRAM ON KEPLER
author: Coleridge
summary: An epigram on Kepler's neglected genius (from the German) followed by fragments of despair, lost love, suicidal weariness, and a passage of Ars Poetica on the making of poetry.

title: EPIGRAM ON THE SECRECY OF A CERTAIN LADY
author: Coleridge
summary: A pointed epigram: a lady said to be secret as the grave is really a grave with a tombstone that tells all; satire of feigned discretion using the imagery of the grave.

title: Epistle to John Hamilton Reynolds
author: Keats
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: A verse epistle moving from chaotic dream-imagery and a Claude-like enchanted castle to a dark vision of nature's 'eternal fierce destruction' seen too far into the sea. It probes imagination, dreams, melancholy, and the cruelty of the natural order.

title: EPITAPH
author: Coleridge
summary: Coleridge's self-epitaph for S.T.C., asking the Christian passer-by for prayer and finding life in death through Christ's mercy.

title: EPITAPH OF THE PRESENT YEAR ON THE MONUMENT OF THOMAS FULLER
author: Coleridge
summary: A learned comic epitaph in the persona of a stout Lutheran mocking Purgatory and original sin while punning on Fuller's wit; satire of theological controversy and the afterlife.

title: EPITAPH ON A BAD MAN
author: Coleridge
summary: A moral epitaph (versions naming Hazlitt) on a man who lived as if he never thought to die and died as if he dared not hope to live.

title: EPITAPH ON A MERCENARY MISER
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epitaph on 'Sell-all', a miser who hangs himself in a dream of giving money away and is doomed to know how many read his tombstone gratis; satire of greed and money.

title: EPITAPH ON AN INFANT
author: Coleridge
summary: Tender epitaph for a dead infant, Death singing it to sleep with a lullaby. Themes of mortality, childhood innocence and grief.

title: EPITAPH: ON HIMSELF
author: Coleridge
summary: A wry self-epitaph composed in sleep, imagining the poet dying as he lived, a-dreaming, alone and unknown at an Edinburgh inn; mortality and self-irony.

title: EPITAPH ON MAJOR DIEMAN
author: Coleridge
summary: A comic mock-epitaph punning on the name 'Dieman' (dead man) and demoting the dead major from Major to 'Corporal' once his soul has gone.

title: EPITAPHIUM TESTAMENTARIUM
author: Coleridge
summary: A self-epitaph giving his sins to Death and the rest to Christ, with a coda on how the heart reveals love it would conceal and absence of love it would show. Themes: mortality, redemption, the concealed heart.

title: eternities
author: Chesterton
summary: Sonnet on the finitude of mortal knowledge against divine infinity: the poet longs for an immortal soul that might finally count the leaves and thank God for all the grass.

title: Ethiopia Saluting the Colors
author: Whitman
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: An ancient enslaved woman, brought as a child across the sea, rises by the roadside to salute Sherman's colors marching to the sea; slavery, emancipation and the war.

title: Eugenics
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Book-length polemic against the pseudo-science of eugenics as a tyranny of the rich over the poor, defending liberty, the family, and the common man against scientific despotism.

title: Europe (The 72d and 73d Years of These States)
author: Whitman
summary: On the 1848 revolutions: the people rise against kings and, though crushed, the martyrs' graves grow seed for freedom; free-verse on revolution, tyranny, martyrdom and liberty.

title: Evening Star
author: Poe
summary: Short lyric preferring the proud distant Evening Star to the cold moon, contrasting celestial lights with the speaker's heart.

title: everlasting man
author: Chesterton
summary: Apologetic history of mankind and of Christ, arguing the uniqueness of man among creatures and of Christ among mythologies; traces the journey from cave-paintings and paganism to the Incarnation and the survivals of the Faith.

title: Excelsior
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse boast in anaphoric questions asserting the speaker's surpassing happiness, boldness and love; themes of pride, joy and the self.

title: EXPERIMENTS IN METRE
author: Coleridge
summary: A set of metrical experiments — weeping into sleep beneath shade, a willow-and-absent-love song, and rustic roundelays of gods following the hare; prosody, pastoral and melancholy.

title: Eyes that last I saw in tears
author: Eliot
summary: Lyric of remembered eyes in death's dream kingdom; grief, division, the golden vision and derision; mortality and memory.

title: Faces
author: Whitman
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: Catalogue of human faces good and grotesque, seeing through their cadaverous disguises to the deific soul behind each, ending in the justified mother of men.

title: Facing West from California’s Shores
author: Whitman
summary: The self as ancient child completing the circle of migration westward yet still seeking the unfound; the quest, the journey, identity, the sea.

title: Faery Songs
author: Keats
summary: Two faery songs: one consoling against tears with the promise of returning blossom, the other a faery's dirge for a dying queen amid falling flowers. They weave grief, consolation, the supernatural, and the cycle of bloom and death.

title: Fairy-Land
author: Poe
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: Fantastical lyric of waxing and waning moons descending over a dreamlike nocturnal landscape, blending imagination, night, and the supernatural.

title: FAITH, HOPE, AND CHARITY FROM THE ITALIAN OF GUARINI
author: Coleridge
summary: A choral translation in which the three theological virtues sing a heavenly minstrelsy of divine love and salvation. Themes: faith, divine love, grace and redemption.

title: Fame, like a wayward Giri, will still be coy
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet personifying Fame as a coy, jilting gipsy-girl who shuns those who court her; reflection on the artist, ambition and the elusiveness of poetic renown.

title: FAMINE.
author: Coleridge
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: A variant fragment of 'Fire, Famine, and Slaughter' preserving alternate readings of the personified Famine and Slaughter dialogue; themes of war's cost, famine and political blame.

title: FANCIES AT NAVESINK
author: Whitman
summary: Eight-part sea sequence at Navesink meditating on tides, ebb and flow, death, rebirth, and the poet's life summed up against the ocean.

title: Fancies Versis Fads
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1923 collection of Chesterton essays defending traditional common sense and wonder against modern fads (psycho-analysis, free verse, prohibition, divorce, evolutionary theory); literary criticism and social satire built on paradox.

title: FANCY
author: Keats
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: Tetrameter lyric praising the roving imagination that, against winter and satiety, conjures all the seasons' delights at once; imagination, the seasons, and the transience of pleasure.

title: FANCY IN NUBIBUS OR THE POET IN THE CLOUDS
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: A sonnet on the shaping power of fancy that makes cloud-shapes at will and ends with blind Homer beholding the Iliad in the voice of the sea. Themes: imagination, the poet-as-prophet, wonder.

title: FAREWELL TO LOVE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Sonnet bidding farewell to Love, to whom the speaker gave his whole heart and whose blindness he caught. Themes of love, disillusionment and renunciation.

title: Fast Anchor’d Eternal O Love!
author: Whitman
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Ecstatic lyric that turns from 'O woman I love' to 'O man, O sharer of my roving life'; comradely love, desire, the sea and the open road.

title: FEARS IN SOLITUDE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: A blank-verse meditation written during invasion fears, moving from a peaceful dell to a jeremiad on England's guilt in war and empire and a chastened patriotism rooted in love of native ground; themes of war's cost, patriotism and nature.

title: femina
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: A short lyric of apocalyptic imagery (black sun, blood moon, thunder) in which a man's stubborn gratitude for the green grass and the love of birds wins a divine commendation; a poem of wonder, faith and gratitude for creation.

title: Fill for me a brimming bowl
author: Keats
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: An early lyric in which the speaker craves wine and Lethean forgetfulness to banish the haunting image of an unattainable beloved; themes of unrequited love, melancholy and memory.

title: FIRST ADVENT OF LOVE
author: Coleridge
summary: A brief lyric likening love's first hope to Eve's first star and a soft south-west wind over Ceres' golden fields. Themes: romantic love, hope, nature imagery.

title: FIRST DRAFT: AN EFFUSION AT EVENING
author: Coleridge
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: Evening effusion invoking Imagination/Fancy to conjure the absent beloved; meditation on memory, hope, love and the sublime storm-imagery of life's wandering way.

title: FIRST DRAFTS, EARLY VERSIONS, ETC.
author: Coleridge
summary: Early drafts of major poems — the Eolian Harp effusion, The Destiny of Nations, the 1798 Ancient Mariner, The Raven, Lewti, Dejection, Hymn before Sunrise, To Wordsworth, Youth and Age; supernatural, nature, imagination and grief across canonical works.

title: First O Songs for a Prelude
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: The opening of Drum-Taps: Manhattan throws off peace and arms for the Civil War, drum-taps and bugles replacing opera; a patriotic mobilization song.

title: Five-Finger Exercises
author: Eliot
summary: Five light verses on cats, dogs, a park duck and self-satire; comic but threaded with time, dust, mortality (all 'come to dust') and the Bread and Wine.

title: Folly’s Song
author: Keats
summary: A refrain song cataloguing comic mishaps and human absurdities, each capped by 'Huzza for folly O!'. It is a festive satire of human folly built on the figure of the fool.

title: FOR A HOUSE-DOG’S COLLAR
author: Coleridge
summary: Two terse epigrams: a watchdog that barks at thieves but not at gallants (satire of marital infidelity), and a Buchanan-derived squib on mutual discredit between poet and detractor Zoilus.

title: For a War Memorial
author: Chesterton
summary: A short epigrammatic war-memorial inscription; the English dead 'died to prove they were not dead', set against the decay of usury and the fall of empires like Carthage. A meditation on heroism, sacrifice and immortality through memory.

title: For Annie
author: Poe
summary: Lyric spoken from a deathlike repose, the fever of 'Living' conquered, soothed by the love of Annie and the peace of the grave.

title: For Him I Sing
author: Whitman
summary: Brief lyric raising the present on the past like a tree, fusing time and space and immortal laws; self-made man as law unto himself.

title: For You, O Democracy
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Programmatic Calamus lyric binding the American continent through the 'love of comrades'; fuses manly comradeship with democratic nationhood in free verse.

title: FORBEARANCE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: A moral-religious poem on forgiving wrongs with humility, drawing on 1 Corinthians 13, with imagery of inner darkness and self-kindled spite.

title: Four Beasts in One-The Homo-Cameleopard
author: Poe
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Satirical sketch of the tyrant Antiochus Epiphanes parading as a beast in ancient Antioch, mocking flattery, tyranny, and mob folly.

title: FOUR QUARTETS
author: Eliot
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: Eliot's meditative masterwork on time, eternity and redemption; the still point, rose-garden, fire and rose, memory; faith, conversion, the quest.

title: FourFaultlessFelons
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A 1930 cycle of four detective stories in which men accused of crimes (a fraud, a murder, a theft, a betrayal) are revealed through inverted detection to have acted virtuously; built on paradox, appearance versus reality, and the innocence behind apparent guilt.

title: FRAGMENT OF AN ODE ON NAPOLEON
author: Coleridge
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: An unfinished ode invoking the Muses and underworld rivers against usurping tyranny (Napoleon), plus domestic and love fragments; classical machinery and political denunciation.

title: Fragment of an Ode to Maia,
author: Keats
summary: An ode-fragment invoking Maia and the old Greek bards, wishing for their 'old vigour' and contentment in simple worship. It treats poetic vocation, classical antiquity, and the immortality of art.

title: FRAGMENTS
author: Coleridge
summary: Short lyric fragments on the grave and the Cherub Hope, and on the wailing sea-mew; brief studies of mortality, hope and seabird imagery.

title: FRAGMENTS FROM A NOTEBOOK
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: A gathering of unfinished notebook jottings (c. 1796-98) of natural imagery, sound, melody and reflection; metrical and imagistic studies later mined for finished poems.

title: FRANCE: AN ODE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: A recantation ode tracing the poet's hope in the French Revolution, his disillusion at France's invasion of Switzerland, and his relocation of true liberty to nature and the individual soul; themes of liberty, disillusionment and the sublime.

title: France (the 18th Year of these States
author: Whitman
summary: A salute across the sea to revolutionary France, the bloody birth of liberty from tyranny; free-verse on revolution, patriotism and democratic hope.

title: Francis Xavier
author: Chesterton
cluster: Martyrdom · The Martyr / Saint · The Cross
summary: A Spenserian-stanza meditation on the missionary St Francis Xavier, whose apparent failure in the East is judged a hidden success by God; themes of martyrdom, faith and doubt, providence, and apparent failure redeemed.

title: frenchenglish
author: Chesterton
summary: A paradoxical essay contrasting French and English national character (candour versus snobbery, revolution versus tradition), arguing that each nation's vices are the flower of its virtues; satire of cosmopolitanism in defence of patriotism.

title: FRIEDERIKE BRUN: CHAMOUNY BEYM SONNENAUFGANGE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: Brun's German ode (Coleridge's source for 'Hymn before Sunrise'): the awed beholder of Mont Blanc asks who set its pillars and torrents, and all nature thunders 'Jehovah'; a sublime nature-hymn of wonder and the presence of God.

title: FROM AN OLD GERMAN POET
author: Coleridge
summary: A Wernicke-derived epigram contrasting German genius with French wit and satirizing German men who father France's foes; national satire touching war and rivalry.

title: From Far Dakota’s Canyons  (June 25, 1876)
author: Whitman
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: A free-verse elegiac sonnet-tribute to Custer's last stand at Little Bighorn, framed as heroic death; themes of war, heroism, the last stand and death.

title: From Montauk Point
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse seascape of restless waves forever seeking the shore from an eagle's vantage; themes of the sea, nature and ceaseless striving.

title: From Paumanok Starting I Fly Like a Bird
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: The poet soars bird-like over the whole continent to sing the idea of the inseparable Union and each of the States; a song of national unity.

title: From Pent-Up Aching Rivers
author: Whitman
summary: Long catalogue singing the phallus, procreation and the desire of body for body; lust, the body, love as inseparable union. Free verse.

title: FROM THE GERMAN
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A short lyric after Goethe's Mignon ('Kennst du das Land'), yearning toward a warm southern land of citrons and myrtle to wander there with a beloved friend.

title: FROM ZAPOLYA
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric song from the play Zapolya: a jewel-bright enchanted bird sings of fleeting May, fading dew and the transience of love's dreams. Themes: transience, love, carpe diem.

title: FROST AT MIDNIGHT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A meditative blank-verse conversation poem at the fireside in which the poet, watching his sleeping infant, moves from memory to a prayer that the child be reared by Nature as God's eternal language; themes of childhood, memory, nature and faith.

title: FULKE GREVILLE: LORD BROOKE
author: Coleridge
summary: Coleridge's quotations from and adaptations of Fulke Greville (used as mottoes and as satirical lines on Napoleon), moralizing on worldliness, divided allegiance to God and the world, and the hollowness of fame and power.

title: Full of Life Now
author: Whitman
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: Closing Calamus poem addressing a reader centuries hence as comrade, the dead poet seeking the living; comradeship, immortality through verse, memory and time.

title: G, H, I
author: Eliot
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Index-of-first-lines fragment (G–I), listing Practical Cats openings and 'Here I am, an old man in a dry month' (Gerontion), 'In my beginning is my end' (Four Quartets) and the Fable's opening line.

title: gargoyles
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: An introductory essay using a parable of the priest of the sun and his three temples to allegorize Paganism, Christianity and modern Realism; a defence of the grotesque and Gothic, with 'man is the ape upside down'.

title: GENEVIEVE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A tender love lyric to Genevieve, prizing not her beauty but the pity and compassion of her soul as the true ground of the poet's love.

title: Germs
author: Whitman
summary: A compact free-verse epigram holding the germs of all forms, worlds and stars within a handful of space; nature, the cosmos, and latent universal life.

title: Gerontion
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: Dramatic monologue of a dried-up old man in a decayed house brooding on history, lost faith and the failed promise of Christ; spiritual emptiness, aridity, doubt and decay.

title: Give Me the Splendid Silent Sun
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A two-part lyric oscillating between a longing for rural solitude and Nature and a counter-craving for the turbulent crowds and drums of wartime Manhattan; Nature vs the city.

title: GKC All is Grist
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A 1931 book of Chesterton essays on slang, divorce, nudism, behaviourism, the Renaissance, Dante, Swinburne and modern fads; satire of fashionable opinion and literary criticism built on paradox and the defence of tradition.

title: GKC Come to Think
author: Chesterton
summary: A collection of Chesterton essays on essays, detective-story writers, the new poetry, the classics, psycho-analysis, original sin and modern claptrap; satire of fashionable modernity and literary criticism built on paradox and orthodoxy.

title: GKC-Autobiography
author: Chesterton
cluster: Martyrdom · The Martyr / Saint · The Cross
summary: Chesterton's 1936 autobiography recounting his Kensington childhood, Fleet Street journalism, friendships and intellectual conversion to orthodoxy and the Catholic faith; built on memory, wonder, paradox and the defence of tradition.

title: Gloria in Profundis
author: Chesterton
summary: A lyric on the Nativity reimagined as a divine descent: God 'falls' deeper than the fallen angels into the cave of Bethlehem. Themes of Incarnation, paradox, and humility through cosmic inversion.

title: God in the Cave
author: Chesterton
summary: An apologetic essay (from The Everlasting Man) on the Nativity in the cave, contrasting Christianity with pagan myth and philosophy, dwelling on shepherds, Magi, and the paradox of God born homeless.

title: Gods
author: Whitman
summary: A litany naming the divine Comrade, the Ideal Man, Death, great ideas, Time, Space and stars as the poet's gods; free-verse hymn on the divine, death, comradeship and the soul.

title: GOETHE
author: Coleridge
summary: Goethe's 'Kennst du das Land' from Wilhelm Meister: Mignon's yearning song for the southern land where citrons bloom, the land of myrtle and laurel; a lyric of longing, exile and nostalgia for Italy.

title: gold-leaves
author: Chesterton
summary: An autumnal lyric on growing old: golden leaves and grey hairs mark the speaker's passage from youthful heroic ambition to humble wonder at ordinary humanity, 'the million masks of God.'

title: Good-Bye My Fancy
author: Whitman
summary: A terse valedictory epigram in which the poet withholds his final word until its proper place arrives at the last.

title: Good-Bye My Fancy!
author: Whitman
summary: The poet's final tender farewell to his Fancy as the clock's ticking slows and the heart-thud stops, hoping the two blended selves go on together to true songs.

title: government
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A satirical essay mocking proposals to standardise private correspondence, defending individual liberty and self-determination against the encroaching claims of the State.

title: Grand Is the Seen
author: Whitman
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: Grand as the visible cosmos is, the unseen soul comprehending and lighting it is grander, more lasting and evolutionary than all the seen.

title: Great Expectations
author: Dickens
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A first-person bildungsroman in which the orphan Pip rises from village forge to gentlemanly 'expectations' funded by a secret convict benefactor; central themes of guilt and conscience, class and snobbery, unrequited love, and the gulf between appearance and moral reality.

title: great-minimum
author: Chesterton
summary: A lyric of gratitude and wonder affirming that to have lived, loved, and seen beauty 'is something' even amid loss; celebrates desire, the mystic rose, and gratitude against a sceptical, jaded age.

title: grocer
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: A comic ballad-song from The Flying Inn pitting the joyous fellowship of the inn against the soulless, mercenary commerce of the grocer; satire of commercialism and praise of feasting and good cheer.

title: GROVE, HIGHGATE SONG, ON HEARING A SONG IN PRAISE OF A LADY’S BEAUTY
author: Coleridge
summary: A short song prizing not the lady's lily brow or roseate cheeks but the gentle look that only Love can see. Themes: romantic love, inward beauty over outward, the eye/look.

title: Growltiger’s Last Stand
author: Eliot
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: Mock-heroic narrative of the bravo barge-cat Growltiger ambushed and made to walk the plank; a comic last stand on the Thames.

title: Gus: the Theatre Cat
author: Eliot
summary: Comic-elegiac verse on an aged theatre cat reminiscing about his palmy days on the stage; nostalgia for past glory and the theatre.

title: Halcyon Days
author: Whitman
summary: Old age's calm, ripe, blissful days valued above love, wealth or victory; serenity as life wanes.

title: HAMLET
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Shakespeare's great revenge tragedy: the Danish prince, charged by his father's ghost to avenge a murder by his usurping uncle, confronts mortality, madness, deception and the gap between appearance and reality in soliloquy-driven blank verse.

title: HAPPINESS
author: Coleridge
summary: A meditative poem weighing ambition against contentment, in which Reason warns against wealth, luxury, and disease, and commends the quiet joys of nature, friendship, love, and humble independence.

title: HAPPY IS ENGLAND! I COULD BE CONTENT
author: Keats
summary: Patriotic sonnet content with England's woods and daughters yet yearning for Italian skies and deeper beauty; patriotism, nature and longing for the South.

title: Hard Times
author: Dickens
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Dickens's condition-of-England social novel set in industrial Coketown, attacking utilitarian 'fact'-worship and laissez-faire economics through Gradgrind's schooling and Bounderby's mill; central themes of anti-industrialism, the deadening of imagination, class conflict and social injustice.

title: Hast Never Come to Thee an Hour
author: Whitman
summary: A brief lyric questioning whether a sudden divine gleam has revealed the nothingness of worldly business, wealth and fashion; a vanitas-tinged meditation.

title: Hemingway — copyright status of acquired vs. excluded works
author: Hemingway
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Editorial/bibliographic note recording which Hemingway works are US public domain (through 1929) versus still in copyright; documents the corpus actually acquired (Three Stories & Ten Poems, in our time, The Sun Also Rises, Men Without Women, A Farewell to Arms) and what was excluded.

title: HENRY V
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Swords and Weapons · The Battlefield · Horse
summary: A patriotic history play following the matured King Henry's invasion of France and victory at Agincourt; framed by a Chorus, it celebrates kingship, national unity, and heroic war while glancing at its human cost.

title: HENRY VI PART ONE
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Early history play dramatizing England's losses in France after Henry V's death, the Joan la Pucelle episodes, and the seeds of the Wars of the Roses (the Temple Garden plucking of red and white roses). Central themes: civil discord, faction, kingship and the cost of war.

title: heret12
author: Chesterton
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: An essay arguing that Christianity's break from Paganism lay not in asceticism but in the mystical, paradoxical virtues of faith, hope, charity and humility; the pagan golden age of reason could not be recovered.

title: HEXAMETERS
author: Coleridge
summary: A verse-letter in experimental English hexameters to Wordsworth and Dorothy, mixing playful prosody with feverish loneliness, friendship and a meditation on the mystery of sight.

title: HEXAMETERS: PARAPHRASE OF PSALM XLVI
author: Coleridge
summary: A hexameter paraphrase of Psalm 46 ('God is our strength and refuge'), a hymn of providential faith in which God stills wars and the heathen rage in vain.

title: HIFTS
author: Chesterton
summary: A satirical short story mocking the Shavian/Wellsian cult of the Superman and the eugenic ideal; the much-heralded Superman of Croydon turns out monstrous and dies of a draught. Satire of progressivism and eugenics.

title: history
author: Chesterton
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A polemical popular history of England from Roman Britain through the Crusades, the medieval guilds, the Reformation and beyond, defending the common man, medieval Christendom and distributist property against Whig and aristocratic narratives.

title: HOME-SICK
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric of exile written in Germany contrasting domestic and natural sweetnesses with the wasting pang of homesickness and longing for Albion's shore.

title: HOMELESS
author: Coleridge
summary: A brief lyric contrasting Christmas as joy for the home-blessed and gloom for the desolate who walks alone through life. Themes: loneliness, exile, memory, grief.

title: HONOUR
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical poem in heroic couplets exposing the vanity of wealth, fame, and modern false honour, dramatizing a rake's repentance that collapses the moment money arrives.

title: Hop-Frog
author: Poe
cluster: Justice / Right and Wrong · Revenge · Avenger
summary: Tale of an abused dwarf jester who exacts fiery revenge on a cruel king and his courtiers at a masquerade.

title: house
author: Chesterton
summary: A Christmas lyric on the paradox of homelessness and home: only where God was homeless, in the stable, are all men at home; the wandering star, exile, and the longing for a truer home.

title: How fever’d is the man, who cannot look
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet on accepting mortal life with temperate calm rather than vexing oneself; uses rose, plum and lake imagery to counsel against spoiling one's salvation by feverish self-torment.

title: HOW MANY BARDS GILD THE LAPSES OF TIME!
author: Keats
summary: Sonnet on the harmonious presence of past poets in the mind, likened to the blended sounds of evening; poetic tradition, memory and the music of nature.

title: How Solemn As One by One (Washington City, 1865)
author: Whitman
summary: Watching returning ranks, the speaker sees behind each mask a kindred soul the bullet could never kill; the immortality of the soul and reverence for the common soldier.

title: How to Write a Blackwood Article
author: Poe
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Literary satire in which Signora Psyche Zenobia receives absurd instructions for manufacturing a sensational magazine 'intensity' article.

title: how-not-to-do-it
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A polemical essay on the right way to argue against Communism, defending private property as the basis of liberty and honour against both Pharisaical and merely acquisitive capitalist arguments.

title: HUMAN LIFE
author: Coleridge
summary: A meditation on the denial of immortality: if the soul dies, human life is a purposeless 'blank accident' of contradiction. Themes: mortality, the soul, doubt.

title: human-tree
author: Chesterton
summary: A lyric on a man who stands tree-still in a field, a Father-figure to nature, while the grass and worms cry to him as to a silent God; themes of stillness, divine silence, doubt and faith.

title: Humanitarianism
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: An essay distinguishing true universal sympathy from the cold, partisan 'inhumane humanitarian'; defends warm moderation born of strong feeling against intellectual anger detached from real human life.

title: Humour
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: An encyclopaedia essay tracing the history of humour from the medieval grotesque through Chaucer, Rabelais and Cervantes to Dickens and English nonsense, distinguishing humour (humility) from wit (justice).

title: Humouresque
author: Eliot
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: After Laforgue: an elegy for a dead marionette with a common, comic face; the puppet as emblem of empty modern mannequins and the mask, half-bullying half-imploring.

title: HUNTING SONG
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A pastoral hunting song from Zapolya summoning shepherds to hunt the wolf and lasses to tend the flocks. Themes: rustic nature, communal labour, the chase.

title: Hush’d Be the Camps To-Day (May 4, 1865
author: Whitman
summary: Soldiers' mourning elegy for the dead commander Lincoln on his burial day, commissioning the poet to sing one verse for the heavy hearts of soldiers.

title: Hymn
author: Poe
summary: Devotional hymn to the Virgin Mary, invoking her grace through joy and the storms of fate at morn, noon, and twilight.

title: HYMN BEFORE SUN-RISE, IN THE VALE OF CHAMOUNI
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
