summary: Sublime devotional hymn before Mont Blanc, summoning the mountain, torrents and elements to utter praise of God. The natural world as a book proclaiming the divine.

title: Hymn to Apollo
author: Keats
summary: A hymn to Delphic Apollo, the speaker fearing he is a worm presuming to wear the laurel and dreading the Thunderer's wrath; classical myth, the god of song, humility and ambition.

title: Hymn to Aristogeiton and Harmodius
author: Poe
summary: Translation from the Greek celebrating the tyrant-slayers of Athens, glorifying liberty, heroism, and the deathless fame of avengers.

title: HYMN TO THE EARTH
author: Coleridge
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: A hexameter hymn after Stolberg hailing Earth as great mother, nurse, and bride of Heaven, a cosmic celebration of fertility, nature and the poet's gratitude.

title: HYMNS — MOON
author: Coleridge
summary: Notebook fragments around a projected hymn to the moon, including the ice-image of Cashmeer, religious devotion, the grave, and a satirical epigram against titled patrons.

title: Hyperion
author: Keats
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Keats's unfinished blank-verse epic on the fall of the Titans and the rise of the Olympians, dramatizing a cosmic succession of powers where the fallen Saturn and Hyperion give way to a new order whose claim rests on superior beauty, and Apollo dies into godhead through knowledge and sorrow.

title: Hysteria
author: Eliot
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: Prose-poem of a man engulfed by a woman's laughter; the grotesque, anxiety, fragmentation and an uneasy fascination/revulsion toward female sexuality.

title: I
author: Coleridge
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Act I of an unfinished historic verse-drama set in Navarre: a returning general, court intrigue, a poisoned conspirator's family, love and revenge, an attempted assassination thwarted by providence.

title: I Because I do not hope to turn again
author: Eliot
summary: Renunciatory penitential lyric of the converting soul giving up worldly striving and praying for mercy; conversion, humility, transience and faith sought amid doubt.

title: I Dream’d in a Dream
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Vision of an invincible 'new city of Friends' ruled by robust love; comradeship as utopian civic ideal, dreams and the city.

title: I Hear America Singing
author: Whitman
summary: Catalogue of working Americans each singing their own song; democracy, the common man, music and song, joyful labor. Free verse.

title: I Hear It Was Charged Against Me
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Poet disclaims destroying institutions, proposing instead 'the institution of the dear love of comrades' across the States; comradeship as civic foundation, democracy.

title: I Heard You Solemn-Sweet Pipes of the Organ
author: Whitman
summary: Sounds of organ, autumn winds and opera are surpassed by the pulse of the beloved heard against the body; love, music and song, autumn, the body.

title: I Saw in Louisiana a Live-Oak Growing
author: Whitman
summary: Emblematic poem of a solitary live-oak that, unlike the poet, can utter joy without a friend near; nature, the tree as token of manly love, friendship and solitude.

title: I Saw Old General at Bay
author: Whitman
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: A vignette of a hemmed-in general calling for volunteers who step forth cheerfully to risk their lives; heroism and self-sacrifice in war.

title: I Sing the Body Electric
author: Whitman
summary: Extended hymn to the sacred male and female body, with the slave-auction section asserting the divinity of every body; the body, soul, democracy, social injustice. Free verse.

title: I Sit and Look Out
author: Whitman
summary: The poet looks out on all the sorrows, oppressions and shames of the world and is silent; free-verse catalogue of social injustice, grief and the witnessing self.

title: I STOOD TIP-TOE UPON A LITTLE HILL
author: Keats
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Early Keats poem of luxuriant nature-description that turns into a meditation on poetic creation and Greek myth (Cynthia/Endymion); celebrates the imagination drawing beauty from the natural world.

title: I The Eagle soars in the summit of Heaven
author: Eliot
summary: Opening chorus: endless cycle of idea and action, knowledge vs the Word, modern London's dust and emptiness; eternal return, faith, spiritual emptiness.

title: I Was Looking a Long While
author: Whitman
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Finding the clue to history not in old fables but in Democracy and the average man of today; democracy, the common man, and the modern.

title: I. The Burial of the Dead
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: First section of The Waste Land: 'April is the cruellest month', the hyacinth garden, Madame Sosostris's tarot and the Unreal City crossing London Bridge; memory, desire, sterility and death-in-life.

title: IAMBICS
author: Coleridge
summary: An iambic metrical experiment promising new heat and light from a praised object; a prosodic study in praise-verse with light imagery.

title: II Lady, three white leopards sat under a juniper-tree
author: Eliot
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: Visionary lyric of dry bones singing under a juniper-tree and the Lady (Virgin/Beatrice) of the garden; Ezekiel's bones, the rose and garden, grace, forgetfulness and spiritual rebirth in the desert.

title: II Thus your fathers were made
author: Eliot
summary: Chorus on building the household of God, the cornerstone Christ, ruined houses and idleness; faith, social neglect, love of neighbour and God.

title: II. A Game of Chess
author: Eliot
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Second section: the gilded boudoir and Philomel, the neurotic dialogue, and the pub talk of Lil and abortion; sterile marriage, frustrated desire, violation and barren love high and low.

title: III At the first turning of the second stair
author: Eliot
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: Purgatorial ascent of a winding stair past the devil of hope and despair toward a sensuous distraction, ending 'Lord, I am not worthy'; penitence, temptation, the climb of the soul and grace.

title: III The Word of the lord came unto me, saying
author: Eliot
summary: Prophetic chorus rebuking miserable cities of designing men who build houses but not the House of God; the Word, satire of modern progress, faith.

title: III. The Fire Sermon
author: Eliot
summary: Third section: the polluted Thames, Tiresias witnessing the typist's loveless seduction, the Thames-daughters and Augustine/Buddha's 'burning'; lust, sterility, the river and ascetic fire.

title: ILN-1930-04-19
author: Chesterton
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: An essay offering corrective maxims for reading the flood of Great War novels and plays, warning against fallacies of sentimentality and 'unthinkable war' slogans; on war, peace and patriotism.

title: IMITATED FROM ARISTOPHANES
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical imitation of Aristophanes' Clouds on the 'glittering Vapors' that feed sophists' fluent speech, plus a fragment on man rushing through infinite space; mocks empty eloquence.

title: IMITATED FROM OSSIAN
author: Coleridge
summary: An Ossianic imitation in which a fading lily by a vale's stream becomes an emblem of transient youth and a lover's voice that lingers as a moonbeam in the beloved's dreams.

title: IMITATED FROM THE WELSH
author: Coleridge
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: Short love epigram in which the lover begs the beloved not to touch his throbbing heart lest it betray his flame; playful lyric of romantic desire.

title: Imitation
author: Poe
summary: Early lyric figuring the speaker's life as a proud, dreamlike tide of vanished hope and visionary thought now passed away.

title: IMITATION OF SPENSER
author: Keats
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Keats's earliest poem, Spenserian stanzas of an idealized lake-isle landscape, plus sonnets on woman and beauty; pastoral fancy modelled on Spenser and Tasso.

title: IMITATIONS: AD LYRAM
author: Coleridge
summary: Translation from Casimir bidding the lyre cease as a storm gathers; meditation on the fleetingness of pleasure, the lyre, summer wind and approaching tempest.

title: improbable story
author: Chesterton
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A fantastical short story in which an overworked, neglected London street rears up to heaven 'for justice'; a parable of the soul of inanimate things, modern bondage to the clock, and wonder.

title: In Cabin’d Ships at Sea
author: Whitman
summary: Addresses his book as a ship voyaging the boundless sea; sea-voyage and open-road imagery, the book as faithful bark. Free verse.

title: in our time (1924 Paris edition)
author: Hemingway
cluster: Disillusionment · Odysseus / Ulysses · Grace Under Pressure / Stoic Endurance
summary: A sequence of eighteen terse prose vignettes (war on the Italian/Greek fronts, the Greco-Turkish evacuation, bullfighting, executions and a hanging) in stripped, imagistic modern style; central themes are war's brutality and aftermath, violent death, disillusionment and stoic endurance.

title: In Paths Untrodden
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Opening Calamus poem resolving to sing only manly attachment and the need of comrades, away from the world's standards; comradeship, identity, nature.

title: In Youth I Have Known One
author: Poe
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Lyric on a youth in mystic communion with Nature drawn from sun and stars, with an appended Paean mourning a young dead beauty.

title: Incredulity
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A collection of Father Brown detective stories in which the priest-sleuth solves crimes by reason and human insight while debunking false miracles and superstition; detective fiction with theological undercurrents.

title: incredulity Fr Brown
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A collection of Father Brown detective stories (Project Gutenberg edition) in which the priest-detective solves crimes through reason and human sympathy while exposing false miracles, superstition and deception; detective fiction with theological depth.

title: innocence
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: The first collection of Father Brown detective stories (The Blue Cross, The Secret Garden, The Invisible Man, etc.), in which the unassuming priest solves crimes by understanding the human heart and sin, often pitted against the master-thief Flambeau; detective fiction with moral and theological insight.

title: INSCRIPTION FOR A FOUNTAIN ON A HEATH
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Pastoral inscription inviting the weary pilgrim to rest and drink at a shaded heath-fountain; a locus amoenus of repose and refreshment for the innocent heart.

title: INSCRIPTION FOR A SEAT BY THE ROAD SIDE HALF-WAY UP A STEEP HILL FACING SOUTH
author: Coleridge
summary: A blank-verse roadside inscription bidding the vigorous youth pity the weary poor wayfarer, and contemplate mortality, charity, and the final rest that wakes in Heaven.

title: INSCRIPTION FOR A TIME-PIECE
author: Coleridge
summary: A meditative inscription on fleeting hours, each parting hour yielding a ghost to dwell within as an 'eternal Now', with attached squibs on Tom Hill and on tears as the eye's language; time, transience, and silence.

title: INSIDE THE COACH
author: Coleridge
summary: A light comic invocation to the god of Sleep to grant rest and dreams to the jolted passengers of a coach crossing Bagshot Heath.

title: Interpolation Sounds
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: Over a funeral service the poet hears interpolated the sudden sounds of Civil War battle, the clamor of arms and cavalry breaking into the solemn rite.

title: intro-love-and-freindship
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A critical-biographical essay introducing Jane Austen's juvenile burlesque; argues she was a born comic genius whose irony springs from controlled exuberance and a satire of sentimental fiction.

title: intro-pilgrims-progress
author: Chesterton
summary: A critical essay on Bunyan and Puritanism, reading The Pilgrim's Progress as a primitive, barbaric, eternal religious allegory of the soul's danger and quest out of the City of Destruction.

title: Irish Impressions
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: The complete nine-chapter text of Chesterton's 1919 travel-essay on Ireland: Irish nationalism and the green symbol, the family and the land, the paradox of labour, the Anglo-Irish and Belfast religious problem, framed by his distributist and Catholic ideals against industrial England.

title: Irish Impressions
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A travel-essay on Ireland during WWI: meditates on Irish nationalism, the Anglo-Irish question, religion, the family and the land, and distributist ideals against industrial England.

title: ISABELLA
author: Keats
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: Narrative poem from Boccaccio in ottava rima: Isabella's brothers murder her lover Lorenzo for money; she keeps his severed head in a pot of basil until she dies of grief; love, murder, grief and the cruelty of commerce.

title: ISRAEL’S LAMENT
author: Coleridge
summary: A translated Hebrew dirge for Princess Charlotte, mourning a young mother and babe lost in childbirth as a rose snapt from its stem, with biblical consolation. Themes: grief and loss, mortality, faith.

title: Israfel
author: Poe
summary: Lyric praising the angel Israfel whose lyre outsings all creation, contrasting heavenly song with the mortal poet's earthbound music.

title: Italian Music in Dakota
author: Whitman
summary: A regimental band playing Italian opera in the wild Dakota night; nature listens, and art and wilderness find unexpected rapport.

title: IV There are those who would build the Temple
author: Eliot
summary: Nehemiah rebuilding ruined Jerusalem with sword and trowel against enemies; faith, perseverance, the bible, building amid opposition.

title: IV Who walked between the violet and the violet
author: Eliot
summary: Vision of the silent veiled sister in Mary's blue restoring the fountains and 'redeeming the time' amid yews and jewelled unicorns; the Virgin, grace, redemption of time and exile.

title: IV. Death by Water
author: Eliot
summary: Short fourth section: Phlebas the Phoenician drowned, his bones picked by a current under sea; mortality, the sea, vanitas and the indifference of death to profit and loss.

title: IX Son of Man, behold with thine eyes, and hear with thine ears
author: Eliot
summary: Chorus rejecting joyless piety, praising the artist who joins his soul to stone in creation; faith, the artist and society, joy, the bible.

title: J, K, L
author: Eliot
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Index-of-first-lines fragment (J–L) listing openings including 'Let us go then, you and I' (Prufrock) and Practical Cats lines; apparatus to the collected poems.

title: Jane Austen GE
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A satirical essay defending Jane Austen as a shrewd psychologist, using Wickham's plausible lying to skewer modern professional politicians and journalism.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Bronte
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Charlotte Bronte's 1847 first-person Gothic Bildungsroman tracing an orphaned, plain governess from abuse at Gateshead and Lowood to passionate love for the Byronic Rochester, the secret madwoman Bertha, flight, and a marriage of moral and spiritual equality; themes of conscience, faith, independence and self-respect.

title: Jealousy
author: Chesterton
summary: A satiric ballad-song mocking a Spiritualist paper's claim that the Catholic Church envies it; the Church personified on her Seven Hills, with mock-heroic religious and historical allusions.

title: JEUX D’ESPRIT: MY GODMOTHER’S BEARD
author: Coleridge
summary: A mythological jeu d'esprit: chaste Pallas grants Mrs. Mundy a beard to repel suitors, with the catch that kisses are barred only until she shaves; comic use of Greek myth to mock female vanity and chastity.

title: job
author: Chesterton
summary: A theological-literary essay reading Job as a poem of paradox in which God answers suffering not with explanation but with wonder, turning scepticism against itself.

title: JOB’S LUCK
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: A comic-satirical epigram (after Logau) on the Book of Job, where the Devil cunningly spares Job's wife and is outwitted by Providence.

title: Jones
author: Chesterton
summary: A satiric comic poem in couplets parodying the relentless overreach of bureaucratic legislation, which dismembers a citizen by acronymic committees in the name of progress and freedom.

title: Journey of the Magi
author: Eliot
cluster: The Journey · The Quest · The Pilgrim
summary: Dramatic monologue of a Magus recounting the hard winter pilgrimage to the Nativity; quest, Birth/Death paradox, three trees foreshadowing the Cross.

title: Joy, Shipmate, Joy!
author: Whitman
summary: A short rhymed lyric celebrating death as a joyful ship setting sail from shore; themes of death as voyage, joy and the sea.

title: JULIA
author: Coleridge
summary: A mock-heroic satirical narrative in heroic couplets in which a courtship is comically ruined when the suitor's kneeling crushes the lady's lapdog, leaving her bereft of both lover and pet.

title: JULIUS CAESAR
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A Roman tragedy on the conspiracy and assassination of Caesar and its bloody aftermath, centred on Brutus's divided conscience; it dramatizes political idealism, rhetoric, fate and omens, and the cost of civil war.

title: KEEN, FITFUL GUSTS ARE WHISP’RING HERE AND THERE
author: Keats
summary: Sonnet in which the cold night walk is warmed by friendship and the remembered poetry of Milton and Petrarch; nature, friendship and literary tradition.

title: KING JOHN
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A history play on the contested reign of King John, dramatizing dynastic legitimacy, political expediency (commodity), the murder of the boy Arthur, and conflict with Rome and France; the bastard Faustconbridge voices its cynical patriotism.

title: King Stephen
author: Keats
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: An unfinished verse history play set during the medieval English civil war between King Stephen and Empress Maud, depicting battle, defiant valour, the question of a usurper's legitimacy, and a king's heroic refusal to yield.

title: kingcole
author: Chesterton
summary: A virtuoso parody-sequence rewriting the Old King Cole nursery rhyme in the styles of Tennyson, Yeats, and Whitman; literary pastiche on mirth, wine and song.

title: KISSES
author: Coleridge
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: Anacreontic myth-conceit in which Cupid distils an elixir named 'Kisses'; light love lyric blending classical mythology and erotic delight.

title: KOSKIUSKO
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: A sonnet lamenting the fall of the Polish patriot Kosciuszko and the death-groan of murdered Hope; themes of liberty crushed, despair, and the cost of patriotic struggle.

title: Kosmos
author: Whitman
summary: Definition of the cosmic person who contains all diversity, body and soul, all globes and eras; the self, the body, nature, and immortality.

title: KUBLA KHAN
author: Coleridge
summary: A visionary dream-fragment conjuring Kubla Khan's pleasure-dome, the sacred river and the Abyssinian maid, ending with the inspired, dread-inducing poet; themes of imagination, the sublime and the supernatural, set in the Orient.

title: L. of G.’s Purport
author: Whitman
summary: Whitman states the purport of Leaves of Grass as celebrating the immortal and the good, ending in sickness, poverty, and old age with Death dogging his steps.

title: La Belle Dame Sans Merci
author: Keats
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: A medievalizing ballad in which a knight-at-arms is bewitched and abandoned by a fairy femme fatale; enchantment, deathly thraldom, dream-vision and destructive love.

title: LA FAYETTE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: A sonnet on the imprisoned La Fayette, figured as a caged matin-bird cheered by his fellows' freedom; dawn imagery promises liberty's triumph over slavery.

title: La Figlia Che Piange
author: Eliot
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: Aesthetic lyric staging an imagined parting of lovers, the weeping girl turned into a pose for the imagination; love, loss, memory and the artifice of art.

title: La Sainte Courtisane
author: Wilde
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: Unfinished verse-drama in which the courtesan Myrrhina and the hermit Honorius exchange fates: she converts in the desert while he turns toward sin, dramatizing faith versus desire.

title: Lady Susan
author: Austen
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: An early epistolary novella whose anti-heroine, the beautiful, scheming widow Lady Susan, manipulates suitors and her own daughter; themes of deception, seduction, marriage as strategy, and feminine cunning.

title: Lady Windermere's Fan
author: Wilde
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Wilde's 1892 society comedy in four acts satirising Victorian morality through the rigid 'good woman' Lady Windermere and the worldly Mrs. Erlynne (her secret mother), built on the fan, the dropped reputation, and an epigrammatic dialogue that dissolves the line between good and bad women.

title: Lamia
author: Keats
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: A narrative poem in heroic couplets in which the serpent-woman Lamia, restored to female form, weds Lycius until the sage Apollonius's cold gaze dissolves her and kills him; enchantment, illusion versus philosophy, and destructive supernatural love from Greek myth.

title: Landor's Cottage
author: Poe
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Descriptive prose pendant to Arnheim, a wanderer's discovery of an exquisitely composed valley, cottage, and landscape-as-art.

title: Landscapes
author: Eliot
summary: Five place-lyrics (New Hampshire, Virginia, Usk, Rannoch, Cape Ann): seasons, birds, decay, the pilgrim's prayer and the white hart; nature, memory, ancient war.

title: last hero
author: Chesterton
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: A heroic ballad in which a doomed warrior, robbed of bride and home, exults in storm, battle and death, loving the rain, his foes and his own annihilation as the last hero who dies the death of God.

title: Laws for Creations
author: Whitman
summary: Ars-poetica laws for American artists declaring man and woman as good as God; the artist and society, the self, and the divinity of the individual.

title: Le Directeur
author: Eliot
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: French quatrain squib lampooning a conservative newspaper editor and his reactionary shareholders over a ragged starving girl; satire of society, class injustice and poverty.

title: Leaves of Grass
author: Whitman
summary: Whitman's master book: a sprawling free-verse epic of self and soul, body and democracy, America, nature, the sea, the open road, comradeship, sex, death and the cosmos. Includes Song of Myself and the Inscriptions; sampling confirms identity, the common man, joy, the sublime, immortality and the book-of-nature stance of the poet-prophet.

title: leisure-state
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A social-critical essay rejecting the mechanized 'Leisure State' utopia; argues that men who do no work become servile parts of a machine, defending the free peasant who controls the means of production.

title: Lenore
author: Poe
summary: Elegiac dirge for the young dead Lenore, the bereaved lover rebuking false mourners and waiting her soul's flight to heaven.

title: lepanto
author: Chesterton
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: A surging narrative ballad of the 1571 sea-battle of Lepanto, casting Don John of Austria as the last crusading knight of Christendom who frees Christian galley-slaves from the Turk.

title: LESSING
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Lessing's light lyric 'Die Namen': the poet asks his love by what poetic name to call her, and she answers that names are mere sounds, asking only to be called 'his'; a witty epigram-song on love and naming.

title: LETTER TO SIR HENRY GOODYERE
author: Coleridge
summary: Donne verse-letter used as a motto for The Friend, figuring the body's morning, noon and night and the soul as a 'larger guest' to whom sun and moon are mere sparks; meditation on mortality and the soul.

title: LETTER, JULY 19, 1802.
author: Coleridge
summary: A short verse variant addressing a poet-friend (Edmund/Wordsworth), invoking joy attuning the soul to nature. Closely related to Dejection's joy passage.

title: LEWTI OR THE CIRCASSIAN LOVE-CHAUNT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: An Orientalised love-lyric in which the speaker, roving by moonlight, vainly tries to forget the unkind Lewti, fading clouds mirroring his lovesick pallor; themes of unrequited love, with moon, cloud and nightingale motifs.

title: LIFE
author: Coleridge
summary: A landscape sonnet in which the widening prospect of the Otter valley becomes an allegory of life's expanding wisdom and a hopeful vision of death as rapturous transcendence.

title: Life
author: Whitman
cluster: The Journey · The Quest · The Pilgrim
summary: The undiscouraged struggling soul of man as an endless march, with an appended elegiac affirmation that all are 'going somewhere'.

title: LIMBO
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: A grotesque metaphysical vision of Limbo, where Time and Space are fettered to a 'last crepuscular half-being' and the worst horror is positive Negation. Themes: time, mortality, the grotesque, privation.

title: Lines
author: Keats
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A sensuous lyric of a lover slipping from his sleeping queen, dwelling on her faery lids and lips amid boundless love; desire, sleep, beauty and amorous reverie.

title: LINES COMPOSED IN A CONCERT-ROOM
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A lyric contrasting the vain, artificial music of a fashionable concert-room with the genuine natural music of song, memory and rustic life, satirizing high-society affectation.

title: Lines for an Old Man
author: Eliot
cluster: The World Upside Down · Madness · Madness
summary: Snarling dramatic lyric of an old man as a caged tiger: wit, blood, the golden eye, madness; age, bitterness and self-knowledge.

title: LINES IN A GERMAN STUDENT’S ALBUM
author: Coleridge
summary: An album verse on student friendship and learning, plus a satirical epigram (after Lessing) on shameless Hippona who cannot blush.

title: LINES IN THE MANNER OF SPENSER
author: Coleridge
summary: A Spenserian-stanza dream-poem in which Love, an archer-elf, conjures a vision of the beloved Sara in sleep; themes of love, dreams, and pastiche of romance.

title: LINES ON A FRIEND WHO DIED OF A FRENZY FEVER INDUCED BY CALUMNIOUS REPORTS
author: Coleridge
summary: Elegy for Edmund, driven to death by slander; grief, calumny, remorse, madness, the grave, and the speaker's brooding on his own kindred fate. Form: elegy.

title: LINES: ON AN AUTUMNAL EVENING
author: Coleridge
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: Reworking of the Effusion: Fancy summons the beloved at autumn evening; imagination, memory, love and the consolations of the native brook and nature.

title: Lines On Seeing a Lock of Milton’s Hair
author: Keats
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: An ode-like lyric venerating Milton as chief of organic numbers and swearing a Delian oath to hymn beauty and immortal song; poetic vocation, immortality of art and reverence.

title: LINES ON THE MERMAID TAVERN
author: Keats
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: Convivial lyric imagining the souls of dead poets carousing in the old Mermaid Tavern; conviviality, wine, the fellowship of poets and a nostalgic golden age of song.

title: Lines Supposed to Have Been Addressed to Fanny Brawne
author: Keats
summary: A brief, intense blank-verse fragment ('This living hand') imagining the poet's hand cold in the tomb haunting the beloved; mortality, the grave and possessive love made tangible.

title: LINES: TO A BEAUTIFUL SPRING IN A VILLAGE
author: Coleridge
summary: Address to a village stream as emblem of memory and past delight, contrasting youthful joy with later turbulence; pastoral lyric on water, memory and mutability.

title: LINES TO A COMIC AUTHOR, ON AN ABUSIVE REVIEW
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A consoling verse to a satirist abused by critics, invoking Momus and Aristophanes to show that mockery is the lot of true wits. Themes: the artist and society, satire, critical hostility.

title: LINES TO A FRIEND IN ANSWER TO A MELANCHOLY LETTER
author: Coleridge
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A consolatory verse-letter urging a friend against melancholy, invoking Fortune's wheel, Time's lyre, and the fall of the despot; themes of mutability, fortune, and consolation.

title: Lines to Fanny
author: Keats
summary: An anguished ode-like address to Fanny Brawne, struggling against obsessive love and jealous memory and longing to soar free; melancholy, desire and the bleak 'hateful land' of separation.

title: LINES TO THOMAS POOLE
author: Coleridge
summary: Affectionate verses recalling fireside companionship of friends jesting, dissecting truth with the 'metaphysic lancet' of Berkeley and Hobbes, and trading puns and riddles; friendship, conviviality, and wit.

title: LINES TO W. L.: WHILE HE SANG A SONG TO PURCELL’S MUSIC
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet on music's power to console at the hour of death and amid misfortune; themes of melancholy, mortality, friendship and the consolation of art, with the music motif.

title: LINES: WRITTEN AT SHURTON BARS, NEAR BRIDGEWATER, SEPTEMBER 1795, IN ANSWER TO A LETTER FROM BRISTOL
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A verse-letter to the absent beloved mingling sea-storm imagery, past melancholy soothed by love, and the electric flash of passion; themes of love, nature, storm, and consolation.

title: LINES: WRITTEN AT THE KING’S ARMS, ROSS, FORMERLY THE HOUSE OF THE ‘MAN OF ROSS’
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Inscription poem praising the philanthropic 'Man of Ross', friend to the friendless and poor; virtue, charity, the common man, and the poet's own sad pilgrimage.

title: LINES WRITTEN IN COMMONPLACE BOOK OF MISS BARBOUR, DAUGHTER OF THE MINISTER OF THE U.S.A. TO ENGLAND
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: An album poem sent with an American minister's daughter, defining country by shared law, language and faith and offering the olive-leaf of brotherly love after the 'fratricidal war'. Themes: kinship of nations, reconciliation, patriotism.

title: LINES WRITTEN IN THE ALBUM AT ELBINGERODE, IN THE HARTZ FOREST
author: Coleridge
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: A blank-verse meditation on the Brocken: sublime mountain scenery that gains meaning from the 'Life within' and from patriotic longing for England, ending in a vision of God everywhere and the world as home.

title: Lines Written in the Highlands after a Visit to Burns’s Country
author: Keats
summary: A meditative poem on the solemn joy of pilgrimage to a great poet's birthplace, and the danger of losing one's mind and the memory of loved faces in such reverie. It treats memory, mortality, the sublime Highland landscape, and the poet as a kind of pilgrim.

title: Lingering Last Drops
author: Whitman
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: A brief lyric on transience and origin: the late poems as the lingering concluding drops of a passing shower, drifting from an unknown source.

title: Lionizing
author: Poe
summary: Comic satire of the 'science of Noses' and literary celebrity, lampooning vanity, fashionable society, and pretentious erudition.

title: litany
author: Chesterton
summary: A devotional Marian lyric meditating on the Incarnation: God grown little, seeing earth through the Virgin as through a window, mirror, and house of gold.

title: LITERAL TRANSLATION.
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: Prose translation and verse variants attached to 'The Destiny of Nations', including Death welcomed by Liberty, the Joan of Arc visions, allegorical war-figures and authorial notes; themes of death, freedom, war, and allegory.

title: Little Door
author: Chesterton
summary: A Nativity hymn (by Frances Chesterton) on the gifts of the Magi, reading gold, incense and myrrh as the sword, battle and honoured death awaiting the sleeping Christ-child.

title: Little Dorrit
author: Dickens
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A social novel centred on the Marshalsea debtors' prison and the child of its long-term inmate, satirising the bureaucratic Circumlocution Office, financial speculation and the imprisoning power of money, pride and respectability; central themes of poverty, social injustice, imprisonment and redemptive humility.

title: Little Gidding
author: Eliot
summary: Fourth of the Four Quartets: a deeply religious meditation on time, fire, the rose, conversion and redemption, set against the London Blitz, ending with the union of fire and rose.

title: Lo, Victress on the Peaks
author: Whitman
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: Address to victorious Liberty after the war, offering not a proud poem but a cluster of night's darkness, blood-dripping wounds, and psalms of the dead.

title: Locations and Times
author: Whitman
summary: A short lyric on the self that corresponds to all places, times, forms and colors; a meditation on identity and the soul's affinity with the world.

title: logic
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A witty essay defending medieval scholastic logic against modern muddled journalism, arguing that thought means disentangling means from ends ('Tennis was made for Man, not Man for Tennis').

title: Long, Long Hence
author: Whitman
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: A prophecy of poetic immortality: only after ages of accumulation and myriad readers will the poet's songs reach their fruition.

title: Long, Too Long America
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: A brief lyric arguing that America must now learn from crises of anguish, not prosperity, to reveal what its people really are; war as national test.

title: longbow2
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A collection of comic-fantastic tales in which impossible English idioms come literally true; eccentric Englishmen launch a distributist agrarian revolution, turning the world upside down in defence of the land.

title: Look Down Fair Moon
author: Whitman
summary: A four-line invocation to the sacred moon to bathe the ghastly swollen faces of the battlefield dead; war-death and mournful benediction.

title: Lord Arthur Savile's Crime
author: Wilde
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A comic society tale in which a young aristocrat, told by a cheiromantist that he is fated to commit murder, treats the prophecy as a moral duty to be discharged before marriage; a satire of fashionable London that inverts fate, conscience and guilt into farce.

title: LordKitchener
author: Chesterton
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: A wartime biography and character study of the WWI general Lord Kitchener, read as a silent epic hero condemned to act an allegory of England's imperial-to-patriotic transfiguration and the raising of the New Armies.

title: Loss of Breath
author: Poe
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: Grotesque comic tale of a man who literally loses his breath, is mangled, hanged, entombed, and revived, parodying horror sensationalism.

title: LOVE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A celebrated ballad-lyric in which the poet woos Genevieve by a ruined tower with the tale of a knight crazed by unrequited love; song, pity and minstrelsy interpret his own desire and win her.

title: LOVE AND FRIENDSHIP OPPOSITE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A short lyric epigram on the irreconcilable difference between love and friendship, arguing love unreturned grows ashamed of itself.

title: LOVE, HOPE, AND PATIENCE IN EDUCATION
author: Coleridge
summary: A didactic poem allegorising Love, Hope and Patience as the three graces who, like Atlas, uphold the little world of Education. Themes: education, the three virtues, patience, childhood and growth.

title: lovers
author: Chesterton
cluster: The World Upside Down · Madness · Madness
summary: A short prose episode from The Poet and the Lunatics: the painter Gabriel Gale, who sees the world upside down to see it truly, woos Diana by asking her to make a rash vow; whimsy, love and madness.

title: LOVE’S APPARITION AND EVANISHMENT: AN ALLEGORIC ROMANCE
author: Coleridge
summary: A late allegorical lyric of despair: the blind Arab figure and a garden-bower vision in which Hope lies dead and Love's kiss only revives death, on lost love and melancholy.

title: LOVE’S BURIAL-PLACE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A dialogue lyric in which the Poet declares Love dead and buried in the lady's bosom, dead of a decline. Themes: love's death, transience, melancholy.

title: LOVE’S LABOUR’S LOST
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Witty courtly comedy in which the King of Navarre and his lords forswear women for study, then fall in love with the visiting Princess of France and her ladies; ends unconventionally with deferred marriage and the song of spring and winter. Central themes: love vs learning, wit and language, the play of appearance and vow-breaking.

title: LOVE’S LABOUR’S WON - A BRIEF ACCOUNT
author: Shakespeare
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Scholarly account of Shakespeare's lost comedy, attested by Francis Meres (1598) and a 1603 bookseller's fragment. As a comedy paired with Love's Labour's Lost it implies themes of romantic love and the fortunes of courtship; the account itself concerns textual transmission and the canon.

title: LOVE’S SANCTUARY
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A short devotional love-lyric enshrining the beloved like a saint in a heart-shrine, treating love as religion. Sonnet-like fragment.

title: Lune de Miel
author: Eliot
summary: French poem contrasting honeymooners' squalid bug-ridden night with the enduring Byzantine basilica of Saint Apollinare; squalid modern flesh against ruined sacred art, decay and transience.

title: L’ENFANT PRODIGUE
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram on a spendthrift 'Jack' whose estate is an algebraic 'quantity less than nothing', mocking debt and extravagance.

title: M, N, O
author: Eliot
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Index-of-first-lines fragment (M–O) listing openings including 'Macavity's a Mystery Cat', 'Midwinter spring is its own season' (Little Gidding) and 'Miss Helen Slingsby'; apparatus to the corpus.

title: Macavity: the Mystery Cat
author: Eliot
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: Mock-detective comic verse on the master-criminal cat who defies Scotland Yard and is never at the scene of the crime; the Napoleon of Crime.

title: MACBETH
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Shakespeare's tragedy of overreaching ambition: spurred by witches' prophecy and his wife, Macbeth murders the king to seize the crown and is consumed by guilt, tyranny and bloodshed; themes of ambition, fate, conscience and the supernatural.

title: Maelzel's Chess-Player
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: Analytical essay using step-by-step ratiocination to prove Maelzel's chess automaton is operated by a concealed human, not pure machine.

title: Magic
author: Chesterton
summary: A stage comedy in which a Conjurer's real magic confounds a sceptic; debates faith, doubt, the supernatural and spiritualism, with fairies presented as mighty elemental spirits.

title: MAHOMET
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: A hexameter fragment celebrating Mohammed as enthusiast prophet-warrior who scattered both blessing and persecution and crushed idolatry, an epic-scale meditation on religion and history.

title: Man Orthodox
author: Chesterton
summary: A wide-ranging anthology of Chesterton essays on humour, the joke, popular philosophy, the Bible, spiritualism, rationalism and the Englishman's religion; orthodox apologetics through paradox and wit.

title: manalive
author: Chesterton
cluster: The World Upside Down · Madness · Madness
summary: A comic-allegorical novel in which the wild eccentric Innocent Smith is put on mock-trial for crimes (murder, burglary, desertion, polygamy) that prove to be exuberant affirmations of life; a celebration of wonder, innocence, joy and gratitude against grey modern pessimism.

title: Mannahatta
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse hymn to New York City celebrating its harbor, crowds, commerce and democratic energy; themes of the city, democracy and America.

title: Mansfield Park
author: Austen
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A novel of manners tracing poor relation Fanny Price's moral growth at her wealthy uncle's estate; themes of class, conscience, marriage, the contrast of true principle with worldly charm, and the maturation of an outsider.

title: manwho
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A cycle of interlinked detective stories whose sleuth, Horne Fisher, 'knows too much' about the hidden corruption of the English governing class; murders are solved but justice is suppressed for reasons of state, giving the book a bleak political-mystery tone.

title: Marina
author: Eliot
summary: Pericles-derived recognition vision of a lost daughter through fog and sea; grace, recovered life, water/ship imagery, hope of new ships.

title: MARK AKENSIDE
author: Coleridge
summary: A blank-verse inscription after Akenside: the traveller is bidden to mourn at the grave of Edmund the learned shepherd, who died of ill-requited love, while faithless Matilda is avenged by Heaven; rural elegy on love, death and pride.

title: Martin Chuzzlewit
author: Dickens
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A satirical novel anatomising selfishness and hypocrisy through the avaricious Chuzzlewit family, the arch-hypocrite Pecksniff and the murderous Jonas, with a sharp comic satire of America; central themes of greed, deception, pride and moral self-knowledge versus self-interest.

title: Me Imperturbe
author: Whitman
summary: Self-poised speaker standing at ease in Nature, self-balanced for contingencies like trees and animals; identity, nature, the sublime calm.

title: meaning of the crusade
author: Chesterton
summary: A chapter from The New Jerusalem defending the First Crusade as a rational, popular religious war and a revolution of the common man; narrates the siege of Jerusalem and Godfrey de Bouillon's heroism, with the cross as central symbol.

title: MEASURE FOR MEASURE
author: Shakespeare
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A 'problem play' / tragicomedy set in Vienna where the deputy Angelo's hypocritical demand for Isabella's chastity in exchange for her brother's life probes justice and mercy, power and corruption, sin, chastity and forgiveness.

title: Mediums
author: Whitman
summary: A prophetic free-verse forecast of future American bards who will report nature and illustrate democracy; themes of the poet as prophet, democracy and America.

title: Meg Merrilies
author: Keats
cluster: Ballad / Ballade · Narrative Poem · The Last Stand
summary: A ballad portrait of the old gypsy Meg Merrilies who lived wild on the moors with the hills as her kin and nature her household. It celebrates the outcast wanderer, nature, and a life outside society.

title: MELANCHOLY
author: Coleridge
summary: Fragment personifying Melancholy stretched on a ruined abbey wall, dreaming troubled dreams; ruins, dreams, melancholy and the grotesque/Gothic mood.

title: Mellonta Tauta
author: Poe
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Satirical epistolary science-fiction set in 2848, a balloon-borne letter mocking democracy, scientific method and human progress; a manuscript-in-a-bottle frame satirizing the future's contempt for the past.

title: Men Without Women
author: Hemingway
cluster: Disillusionment · Odysseus / Ulysses · Grace Under Pressure / Stoic Endurance
summary: A 1927 collection of fourteen short stories (The Undefeated, The Killers, Hills Like White Elephants, Fifty Grand, Now I Lay Me, etc.) exploring masculine codes, grace under pressure, violence, war trauma and the strained or absent relations between men and women, told in Hemingway's spare iceberg prose.

title: mending
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A short essay arguing that mending (restoring a good thing to its ideal) and ending (destroying a bad thing) are opposite acts, illustrated with the Platonic archetype of the perfect armchair; a meditation on reform and ideal philosophy.

title: Mesmeric Revelation
author: Poe
summary: Pseudo-scientific dialogue in which a dying mesmerized man reveals a metaphysics of God as 'unparticled matter,' the soul's immortality, and death as metamorphosis; ends with the sleep-waker's death.

title: methuselahite
author: Chesterton
summary: A satirical essay coining 'Methuselahite' for the modern worship of mere long life; argues the paradox of courage means one must be careless of life to keep it, mocking modern pseudo-religions of self-preservation.

title: METRICAL EXPERIMENT: AN EXPERIMENT FOR A METRE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A metrical experiment in amphibrachs celebrating Freedom's triumph over Tyranny, with scansion notes; a prosodic study fused with a hymn to liberty against idolatry.

title: METRICAL FEET
author: Coleridge
summary: Didactic verse 'Lesson for a Boy' demonstrating trochee, spondee, dactyl etc., closing with fatherly love for his child Derwent. Themes of poetic craft, education and paternal love.

title: Metzengerstein
author: Poe
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Gothic horror tale of feuding Hungarian houses and metempsychosis: a demonic horse embodying a dead rival drives the dissolute young Baron to a fiery, fated doom.

title: midsummer nights dream
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Chesterton's literary-critical essay on Shakespeare's comedy, praising its 'mysticism of happiness', the dream-atmosphere of the enchanted wood, the greatness of the fool Bottom, and its evocation of Merrie England.

title: MILESISCHES MÄHRCHEN
author: Coleridge
summary: German 'Milesian tale' source-poem: a temple on a laurelled headland and a priestess who prays Cytherea's son to guide her lover Kallias by night across the waves to her breast; a classical-mythological erotic idyll.

title: Milton
author: Chesterton
summary: A critical essay on the contrast between the cold, proud, Puritan man Milton and his warm, sensuous poetry; analyses Calvinism, Puritan aristocracy, the Reformation, and Milton's likeness to his own Satan.

title: MINOR POEMS
author: Eliot
summary: Section header containing Eyes that last I saw in tears: death's dream kingdom, lost vision, eyes/tears; grief and the afterlife.

title: Miracles
author: Whitman
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: Catalog declaring every ordinary thing a miracle, from Manhattan streets to the sea and stars; wonder and gratitude, nature, and the divinity of the everyday.

title: Mirages
author: Whitman
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A visionary lyric of mirage-scenes seen at dawn or dusk, vivid spectral images of camps, homes, weddings, and funerals appearing at the sky-edge.

title: misc
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A 1912 collection of satirical character-sketch essays (the Suffragist, the Mad Official, the Free Man, the Mediaeval Villain, etc.) anatomizing social and political types in Edwardian England with Chesterton's distributist, anti-progressive eye.

title: MODERN CRITICS
author: Coleridge
summary: A bitter epigram from Biographia Literaria depicting reviewers as disinterested thieves of reputation and cool murderers of fame; satire of literary criticism.

title: Modern Love
author: Keats
summary: A satiric verse meditation deriding modern love as a dressed-up doll, contrasting trivial dotage with the grand passions of Antony and Cleopatra; satire of love and society.

title: MONODY ON A TEA-KETTLE
author: Coleridge
summary: A mock-elegy lamenting a ruined tea-kettle with funereal pomp, parodying the elegiac monody and praising tea over wine, before Hope consoles with a new kettle.

title: MONODY ON THE DEATH OF CHATTERTON
author: Coleridge
summary: An elegy/monody mourning the suicide of the boy-poet Chatterton, neglected by a hard world; the poet's genius, despair, and dream of an American refuge; themes of grief, the neglected artist, death, and suicide.

title: MONODY ON THE DEATH OF CHATTERTON
author: Coleridge
summary: An elegiac monody mourning the poet Chatterton, who died of poverty and neglect, lamenting the fate of neglected genius and invoking his blessed spirit.

title: morality
author: Chesterton
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: A 1920 essay arguing that negative morality (the Ten Commandments) is really positive, that destruction can be essential to construction, and ending with a meditation on gratitude: 'we love things most when we have nearly lost them.'

title: MORIENS SUPERSTITI
author: Coleridge
summary: The dying husband bids farewell to his wife as Death's bell calls; faith, honour, grief and the widow left in lonely pain. Deathbed lyric.

title: MORIENTI SUPERSTES
author: Coleridge
summary: Companion piece: the dying one is happier than the grieving widow, resting in a remote still world under the providential parent without whom no sparrow falls; faith and consolation.

title: Mormonism
author: Chesterton
summary: An essay using the Mormon scare over polygamy to argue that creeds drive a people's customs, that history is unintelligible if theology is left out, and that the Mormons reproduced an Old-Testament materialist conception of God.

title: Morning at the Window
author: Eliot
summary: Short urban impressionist lyric of damp souls of housemaids and brown fog twisting up the street; modern city, squalor and alienation.

title: MOTTO FOR A TRANSPARENCY
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Road · Napoleonic Wars / the Navy
summary: Occasional verses celebrating the 1814 peace over Napoleon while warning the fettered vulture may break its chain, plus an epigram wishing money had wings to fly to him; war, peace, and money.

title: Mr. Apollinax
author: Eliot
summary: Satiric account of a disturbing, faun-like visitor whose pagan vitality unsettles a polite American teacup society; satire of society, the grotesque and submerged sexuality.

title: Mr. Eliot’s Sunday Morning Service
author: Eliot
summary: Dense satiric quatrain poem on theological pedantry, sterile presbyters and Sweeney in his bath; satire of the church, the flesh-spirit split and learned irony.

title: Mr. Mistoffelees
author: Eliot
summary: Comic verse on the conjuring cat whose magical illusions and tricks delight; joyful light verse on a feline magician.

title: MrPond
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A 1937 collection of detective short stories in which the mild civil servant Mr Pond utters seemingly self-contradictory remarks that prove literally true, each unfolding into a mystery of crime, espionage and logical paradox.

title: MRS. SIDDONS
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A sonnet praising the tragic actress Siddons by likening her effect to a child's terror and pity at ghost-tales of witches and murdered babes; themes of terror, pity, and the theatrical sublime.

title: Ms. Found in a Bottle
author: Poe
summary: A rationalist narrator's manuscript of a doomed sea voyage: storm, a spectral ghost-ship crewed by aged phantoms, and a final plunge into a southern polar whirlpool toward forbidden knowledge.

title: MUCH ADO ABOUT NOTHING
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A romantic comedy of two courtships: the witty 'merry war' between Beatrice and Benedick, and the slandered Hero, nearly destroyed by Don John's deception; it turns on noting/eavesdropping, false report, and the recovery of honour.

title: Mungojerrie and Rumpelteazer
author: Eliot
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Comic narrative of two notorious cat-burglar cats who wreck homes around Kensington; light verse on roguish feline mischief.

title: MURDER IN THE CATHEDRAL
author: Eliot
cluster: Martyrdom · The Martyr / Saint · The Cross
summary: Verse drama of the martyrdom of Thomas Becket: the four tempters, the conflict of spiritual and temporal power, and his death in Canterbury Cathedral as a Christian martyr and christ-figure.

title: MUSIC
author: Coleridge
summary: A burlesque ode that dismisses true Harmony and instead hails the goddess of discordant noise, born of Discord and Confusion, mocking provincial church musicians.

title: MUSOPHILUS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: Stanzas from Daniel's Musophilus, used by Coleridge as mottoes: no state stands sure but on the grounds of right and learning, and 'blessed letters' make the dead live and confer immortality through writing.

title: MY 71st Year
author: Whitman
summary: At twilight the aged poet, like an old broken soldier answering roll-call after the Civil War, reports still alive and saluting the Officer over all.

title: MY BAPTISMAL BIRTH-DAY
author: Coleridge
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: A devotional poem affirming Christian faith and adoption in Christ, triumphing over death where 'Death itself there dies.'

title: My Canary Bird
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse lyric weighing great books against the simple joy of a caged bird's song; themes of nature, the book and joy.

title: My Legacy
author: Whitman
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A free-verse lyric contrasting a rich man's bequests with the poet's legacy of war remembrances bound in songs; themes of mortality, memory and the book.

title: My Picture-Gallery
author: Whitman
summary: The skull/mind imagined as a tiny round gallery holding all the world's tableaus of life and death, with the self as cicerone guide.

title: Myself and Mine
author: Whitman
summary: A defiant free-verse assertion of self-reliance, independence from laws and schools, and the poet's refusal to be expounded; the self, agitation, and democratic individualism.

title: Mystification
author: Poe
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A comic tale of the trickster Baron Ritzner von Jung, master of mystification, who humiliates a pompous duellist with a nonsense treatise and a decanter hurled at a mirror; satire of the duello and honor.

title: Myths and Metaphors
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1929 essay attacking materialists and Darwinians for smuggling a personified 'Nature' into their arguments, and the modern habit of using dead metaphor as a substitute for reason; a satirical defence of clear thought over mythology.

title: Mélange Adultère de Tout
author: Eliot
summary: Self-ironic French poem cataloguing the speaker's many shifting professions and countries; the rootless wanderer, fragmented identity and the artist's self-mockery, ending at his own cenotaph.

title: NAMES
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A light love-epigram after Lessing in which the poet asks what classical pet-name to give his fair one, who answers that names are but air: only call me Thine.

title: NAPOLEON
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Road · Napoleonic Wars / the Navy
summary: Dramatic lines adapted from an old play, contrasting Britain lulled by dreams of peace with the warlike, ambitious Napoleon whose temper is rage, revenge and cunning; on ambition, war and false peace.

title: NAPOLEON
author: Coleridge
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Fragments comparing the sun to a temporising tyrant, on crime corrupting conscience, on the divine Trinity in nature, and a lament for a dead woman; politics, conscience and grief.

title: Napoleon of Notting Hill
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1904 futuristic comic novel set in a drab 1984 London; the joker-king Auberon Quin revives medieval pageantry and the fanatic Adam Wayne fights a war for the sacredness of his little borough, dramatising local patriotism, romance versus rationalism, and the love of small things.

title: Native Moments
author: Whitman
summary: Speaker embraces libidinous joys and consorts with the lawless and shunned, vowing to be their poet; lust, the outcast, the common man, joy.

title: NATURE’S ANSWER
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Stern reproach in Nature's voice asking what was done with the gifts of innocence, hope, health and genius, now returned as guilt and despair. Themes of conscience, the Fall and self-reproach.

title: NETHER STOWEY
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: A conversation poem ('The Nightingale') rejecting the literary conceit of the melancholy nightingale and affirming nature's joy, closing with the poet's hope for his infant son; themes of nature, joy and childhood, with the nightingale motif.

title: Never Bet the Devil your Head
author: Poe
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: A satirical moral tale mocking the demand that fiction carry a moral: the reprobate Toby Dammit literally loses his head to a diabolical old gentleman after wagering it once too often. Satire of transcendentalism.

title: Nevercometrue
author: Chesterton
summary: A lyric song set on the dreamlike island of 'Nevercometrue', where the man and woman that might have been dance and wed; a melancholy meditation on the unlived life, lost love and longing for what never came true.

title: New Fiction
author: Chesterton
summary: A short comic nursery-rhyme parody (on 'Little Bo-Peep') satirising Galsworthy and the fashionable modern fiction of his day; a light verse squib of literary satire.

title: New Jerusalem
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1920 travel book recording Chesterton's journey to Palestine and Jerusalem, weaving impressions of the Holy City with meditations on Christianity, Islam, Judaism, the Crusades, Zionism and the meaning of the pilgrim's quest.

title: new-omar
author: Chesterton
summary: A short parody of FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, mocking the modern teetotal, unfermented-wine puritan whose 'Paradise' is a wilderness; a satirical epigram against prohibition and joyless reform.

title: Nicholas Nickleby
author: Dickens
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Dickens's picaresque social novel following young Nicholas through the cruelties of Dotheboys Hall, theatrical and mercantile London, and the villainy of his uncle Ralph; central themes are the abuse of children and education, social injustice, family, and the triumph of virtue over avarice.

title: Night on the Prairies
author: Whitman
summary: Standing under prairie stars, the speaker absorbs immortality and peace, measures himself by space and eternity, and awaits what death will exhibit.

title: nightmare
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A meditative essay on tales of terror, arguing the imagination may play with horror only if the soul stays upright and Christian; the terror must be 'fundamentally frivolous'. Themes: imagination, the grotesque, faith as anchor.

title: NIL PEJUS EST CAELIBE VITÆ
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A Latin-titled lyric arguing that nothing is worse than a celibate, loveless life, contrasting marriage and affection against solitude, death, and oblivion.

title: NINETY-EIGHT
author: Coleridge
summary: A political-satirical epigram (after Logau) wishing John the Baptist would return to behead Ireland's 'viperous race', alluding to the 1798 rebellion.

title: No Labor-Saving Machine
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Poet's modest legacy is not invention or wealth but 'a few carols' left for comrades and lovers; comradeship, art and the poet's vocation.

title: Nocturne
author: Eliot
summary: Ironic Laforguean sonnet staging Romeo and Juliet under a 'bored but courteous moon'; the poet-puppeteer has Romeo murdered for an effective bloody climax, mocking romantic love.

title: NONSENSE
author: Coleridge
summary: A metrical experiment singing of Jove's bounteous store, of fearless faith amid polar cold and a transfigured radiant joy; prosody combined with a quasi-hymn to providence.

title: NONSENSE
author: Coleridge
summary: A metrical 'nonsense' experiment in dactylic/anapaestic measure singing of Mohammed's story, toil, glory and a merry march to death; prosody as the real subject.

title: NONSENSE SAPPHICS
author: Coleridge
summary: Comic Sapphic verses imitating Horace and Sappho, urging rich patrons to win immortality by patronising the young versifier Gillman; parody of classical form and satire of patronage.

title: NONSENSE VERSES
author: Coleridge
summary: A metrical experiment dismissing fowls of ill presage and welcoming joy, with a wall of flame and pyramid turrets; prosody clothed in festive light-and-dark imagery.

title: Northanger Abbey
author: Austen
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A coming-of-age novel and burlesque of Gothic fiction in which naive Catherine Morland confuses romance with reality at Bath and Northanger Abbey; themes of imagination versus reality, reading, social satire, and maturation.

title: NOT A CRITIC — BUT A JUDGE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: An epigram on the ideal reader-as-judge and a line on sumptuous revenge; brief meditation on criticism, art and the artist's relation to his audience.

title: NOT AT HOME
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A lyric on love and jealousy personified as twin-sisters, treating jealousy as love's inseparable shadow.

title: Not Heat Flames Up and Consumes
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Anaphoric lyric likening the soul's restless burning for the beloved to fire, sea-waves and wind-borne seeds; desire, comradely love, nature and the sea.

title: Not Heaving from My Ribb’d Breast Only
author: Whitman
summary: Anaphoric Calamus lyric of bodily longing ('O adhesiveness! O pulse of my life!') locating comradely love not in the body alone but in song; desire, self and soul, the body.

title: Not Meagre, Latent Boughs Alone
author: Whitman
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: His bare wintry songs may yet burst into future spring leaf and fruit, love and faith blooming like roses.

title: Not the Pilot
author: Whitman
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: The poet declares himself more charged than pilot or pathfinder with composing a battle-call march for the States, years and centuries hence; the poet-as-prophet of the nation.

title: Not Youth Pertains to Me
author: Whitman
summary: A self-portrait lyric: not youth, beauty or learning, but the nursing of dying soldiers and the making of these songs belong to the speaker; the poet as wartime nurse.

title: NOTES BY PROFESSOR SAINTSBURY
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Saintsbury's prosodic commentary on Coleridge's metrical experiments (anapaests, trochaics, dochmiacs, Pindarics); editorial literary criticism of Coleridge as a metrical pioneer.

title: Notes on the Waste Land
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: Eliot's authorial notes citing Jessie Weston's Grail study, Frazer's Golden Bough, Dante, the Buddha's Fire Sermon and Upanishads; a critical apparatus of intertextual and mythic sources for the poem.

title: Now Finale to the Shore
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse farewell bidding the old Sailor depart on an endless cruise beyond return; themes of death as voyage, the sea and the journey.

title: Now Precedent Songs, Farewell
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: The aged poet bids farewell to his earlier songs, naming them as a strange procession born of his life's hot pulsing blood.

title: O Captain! My Captain!
author: Whitman
summary: Rhymed, ballad-like elegy for Lincoln as the fallen captain of the ship of state who dies in the harbor of victory; grief amid public exultation.

title: O Hymen! O Hymenee!
author: Whitman
summary: Brief apostrophe to the god of marriage, the swift fierce moment that would kill if prolonged; desire, marriage, transience, love as near-death.

title: O Living Always, Always Dying
author: Whitman
summary: Lyric on the self continually dying and being reborn, content to leave behind the corpses of former selves and stride ahead, always living.

title: O Magnet-South
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse catalogue poem of nostalgic longing for the American South, evoking its rivers, flora and fauna; central themes are place, nostalgia and nature.

title: O Marie Louise (shew)
author: Poe
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A short lyric love poem on inexpressibility: the poet, who once boasted the 'power of words,' is struck speechless before the beloved's name, standing entranced on the threshold of dreams.

title: O Me! O Life!
author: Whitman
summary: A despairing question about the worth of life among foolish crowds, answered that you may contribute a verse; free-verse lyric on melancholy, identity and meaning.

title: O SOLITUDE! IF I MUST WITH THEE DWELL
author: Keats
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Sonnet preferring solitude amid nature to the murky city, yet crowning it with the converse of a kindred mind; nature versus the city, solitude and friendship.

title: O Star of France (1870-71)
author: Whitman
cluster: Martyrdom · The Martyr / Saint · The Cross
summary: Apostrophe to France as a crucified star and storm-tossed ship, mourning its woes yet prophesying rebirth; figures liberty, martyrdom and resurrection.

title: O Tan-Faced Prairie-Boy
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: A tender camp lyric: a silent prairie-boy recruit who gives nothing but a look worth more than all the gifts of the world; comradeship and tenderness between soldiers.

title: O You Whom I Often and Silently Come
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Confession of a 'subtle electric fire' of unspoken desire kindled near the beloved; desire, the body and silent comradely love.

title: O! I HAVE WAK’D AT MIDNIGHT, AND HAVE WEPT
author: Coleridge
summary: Blank-verse continuation to Charles Lamb: midnight weeping for the lost sister, then hope, faith in the all-seeing Spirit and thanksgiving; grief, faith, friendship.

title: O! Were I one of the Olympian twelve
author: Keats
summary: A fragment wishing for an Olympian decree rewarding the lover's quest after a veiled beauty with ever-ripening kisses. It joins the toil after unattainable beauty with romantic love and Greek myth.

title: oak
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A ballad-song contrasting the enduring sacred oak with the parasitic Lord Ivywood who rots the tree; an anti-industrial, distributist allegory of rootedness vs. destructive modernity.

title: OCCASIONAL VERSES
author: Eliot
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: Section header collecting the occasional/war poems; the present text is Defence of the Islands, a Dunkirk-era patriotic memorial in verse.

title: OCCASIONED BY THE FORMER
author: Coleridge
summary: A political-satirical epigram extending the previous Baptist conceit, wishing the United Irishmen ('locusts') eaten up to save laws and liberties.

title: OCCASIONED BY THE LAST
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram on atheistic 'Jack', warning that after death he will fall foul of howling damnation unless he mends his ways.

title: Ode
author: Eliot
summary: A 'Fair Harvard' valedictory ode: leaving the college's shadow for the importunate years, balancing grief at departure with what is carried away — memory, gratitude and farewell.

title: ODE
author: Keats
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: Ode on the dead poets who live doubly in an Elysian heaven and on earth through their verse; poetic immortality, the afterlife and the teaching power of song.

title: ODE ON A GRECIAN URN
author: Keats
summary: Ode contemplating the frozen figures on a Greek urn and its 'Beauty is truth' message; art's immortality against human transience, beauty and truth, and the cost of stilled passion.

title: Ode on Indolence
author: Keats
summary: An ode in which three urn-like figures, Love, Ambition and Poesy, drift past the indolent speaker who bids them farewell to keep his blissful idleness. It treats indolence, the artist's vocation, ambition, and the Grecian urn.

title: ODE ON MELANCHOLY
author: Keats
summary: Ode arguing that melancholy dwells within beauty and joy themselves, to be embraced rather than drugged away; the inseparability of joy and grief, beauty, transience and mortality.

title: ODE TO A NIGHTINGALE
author: Keats
summary: Great ode in which the bird's deathless song draws the poet toward easeful death and the imagination, then back to his sole self; mortality, transience, the immortality of art and the longing to escape human suffering.

title: Ode to Apollo
author: Keats
summary: An ode imagining Apollo's western halls where the great bards (Homer, Virgil, Milton, Shakespeare, Spenser, Tasso) sing in turn; the poet's pantheon, music and song, classical myth.

title: Ode to Fanny
author: Keats
summary: An ode begging Fanny to keep her heart's pulse for the speaker alone, racked by jealousy and treating love as a sacred religion. Its themes are romantic love, jealousy, and love as worship.

title: ODE TO GEORGIANA, DUCHESS OF DEVONSHIRE
author: Coleridge
summary: A Pindaric ode praising the Duchess for hailing Tell's freedom despite her privileged birth, contrasting aristocratic luxury with the toiler's misery and celebrating maternal love and social liberty.

title: ODE TO PSYCHE
author: Keats
summary: Ode building a shrine to the late-born goddess Psyche within the poet's own mind; classical myth, love (Cupid and Psyche), and the imagination as the true temple of the divine.

title: ODE TO THE DEPARTING YEAR
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: A Pindaric ode lamenting the bloodshed of 1796, prophesying divine judgement on warring tyrants and on England; themes of providence, war's cost and patriotic dread for Albion.

title: ODE TO TRANQUILLITY
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: An ode invoking Tranquillity above Fame, contrasting calm contemplative nature with the feverish, blood-and-guile 'trade' of present men, a retreat into philosophic peace.

title: OF BALIOL COLLEGE, OXFORD, AUTHOR OF THE ‘RETROSPECT’, AND OTHER POEMS
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet to Southey whose melodies wake memory and hope; dwells on the bittersweet pleasure of recollected past delight; themes of memory, friendship, and poetry.

title: Of Him I Love Day and Night
author: Whitman
summary: Dream of searching burial-places for a dead beloved and finding every place full of the dead; resolves to dispense with graves, content with death everywhere.

title: OF HUMANE LEARNING
author: Coleridge
summary: Stanza from Fulke Greville used by Coleridge as a motto on learning and faith, arguing that true understanding lives only where knowledge breeds obedience and works.

title: Of That Blithe Throat of Thine
author: Whitman
summary: The poet takes the arctic bird's gay song as a lesson, singing cheerfully even amid the winter of old age.

title: Of the Awefull Battle of the Pekes and the Pollicles
author: Eliot
summary: Mock-heroic comic battle of dogs broken up by the Great Rumpuscat; light verse parodying tribal warfare among pets.

title: Of the Terrible Doubt of Appearances
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Philosophical Calamus poem where epistemological doubt (appearance vs reality, identity beyond the grave) is answered not by reason but by the touch of the beloved comrade.

title: Oh, I am frighten’d with most hateful thoughts!
author: Keats
summary: A fragment in which the lover frets that his idealized beloved may have ordinary flaws, comparing her to Dian and Juno. It treats romantic idealization, doubt, and appearance versus reality.

title: Old Age’s Lambent Peaks
author: Whitman
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: A late valedictory lyric celebrating the elevated, illuminating vista of old age at life's golden twilight, where calmer perspective reveals the best of experience.

title: Old Age’s Ship & Crafty Death’s
author: Whitman
summary: Old age and death imagined as rival vessels closing in, met with defiant joy of strife as the poet's ship crowds on full sail toward the open sea.

title: Old Chants
author: Whitman
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A roll-call of the world's ancient poets and epics from Egypt, the Bible, Greece, and medieval legend, acknowledging America's debt to old poems and traditions.

title: Old Deuteronomy
author: Eliot
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Comic verse on the ancient village cat who has lived many lives in succession and is revered by all; gently touches age and the nine lives.

title: Old Ireland
author: Whitman
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: Allegory of Ireland as a grieving ancient mother over an empty grave, consoled that her dead son lives risen in a new country; grief, resurrection, exile, and rebirth in America.

title: OLD POSSUM’S BOOK  OF PRACTICAL CATS
author: Eliot
summary: Collection header for Eliot's light comic verse about cats; opens with The Naming of Cats on the inscrutable third name each cat keeps secret.

title: Old Salt Kossabone
author: Whitman
summary: A narrative of an old sailor ancestor who dies at his window the moment he sees a ship win free to the open sea.

title: Old War-Dreams
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: A free-verse lyric with refrain recounting recurring nightmares of the Civil War dead; themes of war's cost, dreams, memory and death.

title: oldsong
author: Chesterton
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: An apocalyptic ballad of London Bridge broken down, the kings who 'buy and sell', and Cobbett as the Horseman of Apocalypse; a populist, anti-plutocratic vision of England renewed.

title: Oliver Twist
author: Dickens
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
