title: The Singer in the Prison
author: Whitman
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: A lady sings a redeeming hymn to convicts about the imprisoned soul freed by the pardoner death; music, sin, grace, the body, and death as deliverance.

title: The Sleeper
author: Poe
summary: A nocturnal lyric meditating on a beautiful dead (or deathly sleeping) woman, Irene, beneath the mystic moon; her sleep merges with the grave. Themes of death, the dead beloved, sleep and melancholy.

title: The Sleepers
author: Whitman
summary: Long dream-journey through the night in which the wandering soul merges with all sleepers and dreamers; death, night and sleep level and reconcile humanity.

title: THE SNOW-DROP
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric addressed to a snowdrop made immortal by Laura's (Mrs. Robinson's) song, bearing it to Pierian climes where the Phoenix nests and Lethe steals, a poem of art's immortality and memory.

title: The Sobbing of the Bells (Midnight, Sept. 19-20, 1881)
author: Whitman
summary: A brief free-verse elegy on the tolling bells announcing President Garfield's death and the nation's grief; themes of death, bells, the nation and mourning.

title: The Song of the Jellicles
author: Eliot
summary: Lilting song of the Jellicle Cats dancing by the light of the Jellicle Moon at the Jellicle Ball; joyful nocturnal dance verse.

title: The Song of the Wheels
author: Chesterton
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A militant ballad in which industrial machines stand silent in protest and the dispossessed workmen confront 'King Dives' in his iron garden. Themes: class conflict, the dehumanizing tyranny of the machine, and social revolt.

title: The Soul of Man under Socialism
author: Wilde
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Political-aesthetic essay arguing that abolishing private property frees a true Individualism, attacking poverty, charity, authority and public opinion, and championing the artist's autonomy from society.

title: The Speaker
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A literary-critical review of the letters and poems of the Manx poet T. E. Brown, meditating on friendship, the privacy of private letters, and frivolity as something sacred. Themes: friendship, the artist and his work, and reflection on death and judgment.

title: The Sphinx
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A short tale set during a cholera epidemic in which the narrator, sick with dread, mistakes a tiny death's-head moth on a windowpane for a monstrous distant apparition; a parable of misjudged proximity and the mind's terror. Themes of terror, omens, appearance vs reality.

title: The Sphinx
author: Wilde
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: Wilde's decadent narrative poem in which a student addresses an immortal Egyptian Sphinx, conjuring her ancient lovers and exotic gods amid lust, decay and ruin, before recoiling toward his crucifix at the close.

title: The Sphinx Without a Secret
author: Wilde
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: Short story of an enigmatic woman whose 'mystery' proves empty; a Sphinx without a secret, exploring appearance versus reality, secrecy and unrequited love.

title: The Star-Child
author: Wilde
summary: A fairy tale of a beautiful but proud and cruel foundling who, punished with ugliness for denying his beggar mother, undergoes a penitential quest of humility and charity, is restored, and redeemed in an explicitly Christ-toned arc of fall, suffering and redemption.

title: The Sun Also Rises
author: Hemingway
cluster: Disillusionment · Odysseus / Ulysses · Grace Under Pressure / Stoic Endurance
summary: Hemingway's 1926 modernist novel of the post-WWI 'Lost Generation': expatriate Americans and Britons drinking through Paris and the Pamplona bullfight fiesta, narrated by the war-wounded, impotent Jake Barnes, whose hopeless love for Brett Ashley dramatizes disillusionment, aimlessness, and spiritual emptiness rendered in terse, understated prose.

title: The System of Doctor Tarr and Professor Fether
author: Poe
cluster: The World Upside Down · Madness · Madness
summary: A satirical horror-comedy: a visitor to a French madhouse discovers the lunatics have overthrown their keepers and taken over the asylum. Themes of madness, the world upside down, and appearance vs reality.

title: THE TAMING OF THE SHREW
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: Robust early Shakespearean comedy verging on farce: Petruccio woos and 'tames' the shrewish Katherine while disguised suitors compete for Bianca, framed by the Christopher Sly induction that explores persuasion, appearance vs reality, and the play-within-the-play.

title: THE TASTE OF THE TIMES
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram on the fashion for premature talent and child prodigies, punning on a 'petty Pitt'; satire of contemporary taste and celebrity.

title: THE TEARS OF A GRATEFUL PEOPLE
author: Coleridge
summary: A translated Hebrew dirge and hymn for the funeral of King George III, mourning a just king as a fallen day-star and praying for the royal line. Themes: grief and loss, kingship, faith, providence.

title: The Tell-Tale Heart
author: Poe
cluster: The World Upside Down · Madness · Madness
summary: A first-person tale of a mad narrator who murders an old man over his 'vulture eye', dismembers the body, then is undone by the imagined beating of the dead man's heart. Themes of madness, guilt, conscience and terror.

title: THE TEMPEST
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Shakespeare's late romance on the magician Prospero, exiled duke who raises a storm to bring his usurpers to his island, tests the lovers Ferdinand and Miranda, and finally forgives; central are magic and the supernatural, usurpation, forgiveness, nature versus civilization, and art.

title: The Tenant of Wildfell Hall
author: Bronte
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Anne Bronte's 1848 novel, framed as Gilbert Markham's narrative enclosing Helen Graham's diary, in which a wife flees her dissolute, alcoholic and abusive husband Arthur Huntingdon to protect herself and her son; a morally bold social novel on marriage, debauchery, a woman's independence, faith and redemption.

title: The Terror of a Toy
author: Chesterton
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A satirical essay mocking the fad of banning toy bows and cannons, arguing that danger lies in the child not the implement and that the toy sword is 'the soul of the sword that will never be stained with blood'. Themes: satire of progressive faddism, common sense, and the poetry of arms and heroism.

title: The Thing
author: Chesterton
summary: A collection of apologetic essays defending Catholic orthodoxy ('Why I Am a Catholic') against scepticism, humanism, and the Protestant and modern drift. Themes: faith and the defence of dogma, conversion and orthodoxy, and critique of fashionable progress.

title: The Thousand-And-Second Tale of Scheherazade
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A satirical frame-tale extending the Arabian Nights: Scheherazade tells of Sindbad's encounters with modern marvels of science, which the incredulous king finds too improbable, and has her executed. Themes of truth stranger than fiction, satire and wonder.

title: THE THREE GRAVES
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A ballad-tale of a mother who, enamoured of her daughter's suitor, lays a curse that blights the marriage; a psychological study of jealousy, guilt and a mother's malediction; themes of jealousy, guilt and the supernatural.

title: THE THREE SORTS OF FRIENDS
author: Coleridge
summary: A witty epigram dividing friends into ac-, con- and in-quaintance (from his child's coinage) plus a fragment on inward beauty of womanhood; friendship and grace.

title: The Torch
author: Whitman
summary: Imagist miniature of Northwest fishermen spearing salmon by torchlight at night on a black lake; pure nocturnal image of fire on water.

title: THE TRAGEDY OF KING LEAR - THE FOLIO TEXT
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Shakespeare's great tragedy in blank verse on the aged King Lear who divides his kingdom by flattery, descends into madness and the storm, and is broken by filial ingratitude; central are kingship, the natural order, madness, suffering, and the question of justice in a pitiless world.

title: The Truth of Masks
author: Wilde
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Wilde's critical essay on Shakespeare's use of costume and illusion, arguing that archaeological accuracy is a method of artistic illusion and ending on the paradox that the truths of metaphysics are the truths of masks.

title: THE TWO FOUNTS
author: Coleridge
summary: Stanzas to a suffering lady whose beauty dispenses only cheer; a dream-dwarf explains the two inner founts of Suffering and Cheer since Adam's sin. Themes: suffering, beauty, the fall, compassion.

title: THE TWO GENTLEMEN OF VERONA
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Early Shakespearean romantic comedy in which the friends Valentine and Proteus both fall for Silvia; centres on the conflicting claims of love and friendship, fidelity vs betrayal, courtly love and disguise (Julia following Proteus dressed as a boy).

title: THE TWO NOBLE KINSMEN
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A late tragicomic romance (with Fletcher) from Chaucer's Knight's Tale, in which kinsmen Palamon and Arcite, sworn friends, fall in love with Emilia and fight to the death for her; themes are the conflict of love and friendship, fortune's paradoxes, and chivalric ritual.

title: THE TWO ROUND SPACES ON THE TOMBSTONE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Grotesque · Good vs Evil · Satanic Figure
summary: A grotesque satirical ballad-lampoon in which the Devil and his grandam sit on a churchyard tombstone awaiting a buried 'Counsellor', a venomous personal attack steeped in diabolic and graveyard imagery.

title: The Unexpress’d
author: Whitman
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: After all the world's poetry from Homer to Shakespeare, the poet wonders whether the best still remains unexpressed and lacking, a topos of inexpressibility.

title: The United States to Old World Critics
author: Whitman
summary: America answers European critics by pointing to its concrete daily building of a vast perpetual edifice rising to the stars.

title: The Unparalleled Adventures of one Hans Pfaall
author: Poe
cluster: The Journey · The Quest · The Pilgrim
summary: A proto-science-fiction hoax-tale: a bankrupt Rotterdam bellows-mender escapes his debts by ballooning to the Moon, narrated with pseudo-scientific detail. Themes of the quest, the journey, satire and wonder.

title: The Uses of Diversity
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1920 collection of light familiar essays on literature, society, religion and modern fads, defending wonder, paradox and orthodoxy against pseudo-scientific seriousness; satirical social criticism in the essay form.

title: The Valley of Unrest
author: Poe
summary: A short lyric on a once-peaceful dell, now restless and weeping over a nameless grave after its people went to the wars. Themes of death, mutability, melancholy and a haunted landscape.

title: The Village Street
author: Poe
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A melancholic narrative lyric: a nocturnal walk with a scornful maiden ends in parting and lifelong heartbreak, the once-pleasant elms now whispering mad, discordant melodies. Themes of lost love, melancholy and memory.

title: THE VIRGIN’S CRADLE-HYMN
author: Coleridge
summary: A short Latin cradle-hymn of the Virgin Mary singing the sleeping infant Jesus, copied from a Catholic print. Themes of divine love, the Virgin and childhood in hymn form.

title: THE VISIONARY HOPE
author: Coleridge
summary: Lyric of a sick man with no hope but one love-stricken visionary hope, sleep dreaded for its screams. Themes of despair, sickness, hope and love's despair as hope's ghost.

title: THE VISIT OF THE GODS: IMITATED FROM SCHILLER
author: Coleridge
summary: A Bacchic ode after Schiller in which the Olympian gods descend on the poet, who drinks the nectar of inspiration that 'forbids me to die', a rapture of poetic immortality.

title: The Voice of the Rain
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: The rain answers the poet as the 'Poem of Earth', an eternal cycle of rising and returning likened to song.

title: The Wallabout Martyrs
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: Elegy for Revolutionary War prison-ship dead, ranked above classical heroes as the foundation stones of America.

title: THE WANDERINGS OF CAIN
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Outsider · Fall from Innocence · The (Reputed) Fallen Woman
summary: Canto II of the prose-poem in which Cain, led by his innocent child Enos through a dark forest, cries out under relentless divine persecution and longs for death; themes of guilt, sin and the fall, and the outcast wanderer.

title: THE WANDERINGS OF CAIN
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Outsider · Fall from Innocence · The (Reputed) Fallen Woman
summary: A prose-poem fragment (prefatory note and plan) on the guilt-haunted, God-pursued wanderings of Cain after Abel's murder; themes of sin and the fall, guilt and the outcast wanderer, drawing on the Bible.

title: THE WASTE LAND  1922
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: Title/epigraph page of Eliot's epoch-defining long poem (Sibyl epigraph, dedication to Pound); a fragmentary modernist epic of spiritual desolation, sterility and the ruined post-war city.

title: THE WILLS OF THE WISP
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A Sapphic lyric in which deceiving will-o'-the-wisps that lure the traveller into the swamp are likened to a woman's perfidious glances; the supernatural and the femme fatale as deceiver.

title: The wind sprang up at four o’clock
author: Eliot
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: Lyric of wind breaking bells, swinging between life and death; the blackened river, death's other kingdom, Tartar horsemen; death and the uncanny.

title: THE WINTER’S TALE
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A late dramatic romance in which Leontes' irrational jealousy destroys his family, followed across sixteen years by pastoral renewal and the wondrous restoration of the lost daughter Perdita and the statue-like Hermione; its themes are jealousy, repentance, time, and redemptive grace.

title: the wise men
author: Chesterton
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: A Nativity lyric in which the three wise men, masters of all learning but truth, are humbled before the Christ-child; celebrates wonder, humility and the Incarnation over arid intellectualism.

title: The World below the Brine
author: Whitman
summary: A catalogue of the strange life of the ocean floor and its passions and wars, paralleling change between spheres of being; free-verse lyric on the sea, nature and metempsychosis.

title: The Wound Dresser: A Series of Letters Written from the Hospitals in Washington during the War of the Rebellion
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: Whitman's Civil War letters and hospital memoranda from Washington DC, recording his nursing of wounded and dying soldiers and the human cost of the war. The text centers on death, suffering, comradeship, and the dignity of the common soldier, written in plain epistolary autobiographical prose.

title: The Wound-Dresser
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: An old man recalls tending the wounded and dying in army hospitals, dressing terrible wounds with impassive hand and burning heart; compassion, suffering and the human cost of war.

title: The Young King
author: Wilde
cluster: Martyrdom · The Martyr / Saint · The Cross
summary: A fairy-tale allegory in which a beauty-loving young king, taught by three dreams of the suffering behind his coronation finery, renounces luxury and is crowned by divine light as a Christ-like figure.

title: the-englishman
author: Chesterton
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: A comic patriotic song invoking St George, English ale, beef and chivalry; nationalism, food and drink, the dragon-slaying hero.

title: TheAppOfTyranny
author: Chesterton
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A 1915 polemical war essay arguing that Prussian militarism is a deliberate barbarism at war with civilisation; defends the Allied cause against tyranny in WWI.

title: TheCrimesOfEngland
author: Chesterton
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: A 1916 satirical historical-polemical essay charging England's real crime as its long collusion with Prussia; an ironic patriotic critique tied to the First World War.

title: There Was a Child Went Forth
author: Whitman
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: Catalog of a child becoming everything he beholds, from lilacs and farm animals to parents and the city; identity, childhood, perception, and the merging of self and world.

title: These I Singing in Spring
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Spring-walk poem of the 'poet of comrades' gathering natural tokens (the calamus-root) for lovers; nature, love, friendship and memory of the dead in free verse.

title: Thick-Sprinkled Bunting
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: A free-verse apostrophe to the American flag prophesying its supremacy over the flags of kings; themes of patriotism, democracy and the flag of man.

title: This Compost
author: Whitman
summary: Awe and terror at the earth's chemistry that grows sweet spring crops out of diseased corpses; death, decay, regeneration, nature, and resurrection of the grass.

title: This Dust Was Once the Man
author: Whitman
summary: Epitaph-quatrain for Lincoln, the gentle resolute man who saved the Union against the foulest crime in history; mortality, dust, and martyrdom.

title: THIS LIME-TREE BOWER MY PRISON
author: Coleridge
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: A blank-verse conversation poem in which the disabled poet imaginatively follows his friends through the landscape, discovering that nature never deserts the wise; themes of imagination, nature and friendship.

title: This Moment Yearning and Thoughtful
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Poet imagining brethren and lovers yearning in other lands; comradeship extended into international, cosmopolitan brotherhood.

title: Thou Art the Man
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A comic detective/ratiocination tale: the narrator unmasks 'Old Charley Goodfellow' as the murderer of his friend by springing the corpse from a wine-box to cry 'Thou art the man'. Themes of detection, guilt, deception and appearance vs reality.

title: Thou Mother with Thy Equal Brood
author: Whitman
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: Prophetic ode to America as the great Mother and ship of Democracy, blending body and soul, fusing past nations and pointing to a spiritual future Union.

title: Thou Orb Aloft Full-Dazzling
author: Whitman
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: Invocation to the October noon sun as fructifying lover, asking it to shed its ray on the poet's chants and prepare his lengthening shadows and starry nights.

title: Thought
author: Whitman
summary: At a feast a spectral vision of a shipwreck at sea (the steamship Arctic) prompts the anguished question whether souls are drowned and matter alone triumphant.

title: Thought
author: Whitman
summary: Satiric meditation on people of high position whose attainments sink away, mocking false realities and rotten core happiness; vanitas, the self, and critique of society.

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse catalogue on public opinion, the fall of corrupt officials and the rise of the democratic New World; themes of democracy and the common man.

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: A two-part free-verse meditation on America's birth-pangs, the war's price and the westward seeds of the future; themes of democracy, the West and transition through death.

title: Thoughts
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: A brief free-verse meditation on ownership, vista and the ever-continued journey toward what will yet be supplied; the open road, progress and the self.

title: THOUSAND HUMAN BEINGS, MEN, WOMEN, AND CHILDREN, MURDERED IN COLD BLOOD,
author: Coleridge
summary: Prose note and textual apparatus to the Ode to the Departing Year, condemning the Empress of Russia's atrocities and Britain's complicity in war, slavery and famine, citing the prophet Nahum.

title: Three Stories & Ten Poems
author: Hemingway
cluster: Disillusionment · Odysseus / Ulysses · Grace Under Pressure / Stoic Endurance
summary: Hemingway's 1923 debut: three terse, plainspoken short stories (sexual disillusionment in rural Michigan, a failed fishing outing and strained marriage in the Italian Alps, a boy's love for his crooked jockey father who dies on the track) plus ten poems dominated by war, soldiers' deaths, the sea, suicide and lost youth. Central themes: disillusionment, loss of innocence, mortality and the cost of war, rendered in his early stripped-down style.

title: TIME, REAL AND IMAGINARY
author: Coleridge
summary: An allegory in which two children (a sighted sister, a blind brother) race endlessly on a faery mountain, figuring imaginary versus real time. Central themes: time, memory, the imagination.

title: TIMON OF ATHENS
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A bitter, schematic tragedy/satire in which the lavishly generous Timon, abandoned by flattering friends once his wealth fails, turns misanthrope and curses humanity from the wilderness; themes of money, false friendship, ingratitude and misanthropy.

title: titanic
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1912 essay reading the Titanic disaster as an analogy for modern civilisation and the State: overgrown, complacent, divided by class; meditation on death, courage and corporate conscience.

title: titanicGKC
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A ballade written for a 1912 Titanic benefit, insisting that beneath theatrical illusion 'there are real things' — death, courage and human reality break through the unreal.

title: TITUS ANDRONICUS
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Justice / Right and Wrong · Revenge · Avenger
summary: Bloody Senecan revenge tragedy set in late Rome: the cycle of mutilation, rape and cannibalistic vengeance between Titus and Tamora. Central themes: revenge, the grotesque and horror, justice and barbarism.

title: TO * * * * * *
author: Keats
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Petrarchan-style sonnet of romantic longing in which the speaker, lacking knightly beauty, woos by spells and incantation; unrequited desire and fancy.

title: TO * * * *
author: Keats
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Lyric blazon praising a woman's beauty and imagining her as an enchantress in days of chivalry; romantic compliment fused with medieval fancy.

title: To --
author: Poe
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A short love lyric of dream-visions: the beloved's lips, melody and heart haunt the speaker's sleep, set against the worthlessness of gold. Themes of love, dreams and longing.

title: To --
author: Poe
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A brief love lyric in which the speaker, indifferent to his own desolate lot, is moved that the beloved should sorrow for a mere passer-by. Themes of love, melancholy and transience.

title: To a Certain Cantatrice
author: Whitman
summary: Gift reserved for a hero or rebel is bestowed instead on a singer; music and song, the cause of freedom, the rebel/common artist.

title: To a Certain Civilian
author: Whitman
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A defiant address rejecting the civilian's wish for soft rhymes, affirming the poet's martial, war-born art and his role as singer of the funeral dirge.

title: TO A CHILD
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A light playful occasional verse addressed to a small girl ('Little Miss Fanny'); celebrates childhood, mirth and innocence in a brief comic lyric.

title: To a Common Prostitute
author: Whitman
cluster: The Outsider · Fall from Innocence · The (Reputed) Fallen Woman
summary: Compassionate, scandalous address welcoming the prostitute as Nature welcomes all; the outcast, social injustice, the body, and radical acceptance.

title: TO A CRITIC
author: Coleridge
summary: A literary-satirical epigram retorting against a critic who quoted a passage out of context, threatening to pull out the critic's eye as 'analytic.'

title: To a Foil’d European Revolutionaire
author: Whitman
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: Consolation to a defeated revolutionary that Liberty waits latent and is the last to leave; revolution, martyrs, defeat made great, and undying liberty.

title: TO A FRIEND
author: Coleridge
summary: Blank-verse epistle to Charles Lamb tending his sick sister, and the poet recalling his own lost sister; friendship, grief, the sister, tenderness.

title: TO A FRIEND: (CHARLES LAMB) WHO HAD DECLARED HIS INTENTION OF WRITING NO MORE POETRY
author: Coleridge
summary: A blank-verse epistle to Charles Lamb invoking classical Muses and Burns's neglected death to urge his friend not to abandon poetry; themes of friendship, vocation and the artist.

title: TO A FRIEND WHO SENT ME SOME ROSES
author: Keats
summary: Sonnet on a gift of roses whose fragrance whispers peace and friendliness; the rose as emblem of friendship and reconciliation in a nature setting.

title: To a Historian
author: Whitman
summary: Opposes the historian of surfaces with himself as chanter of personality projecting the history of the future; prophet-poet, identity, the common man.

title: TO A LADY WITH FALCONER’S SHIPWRECK
author: Coleridge
summary: A verse epistle accompanying the gift of Falconer's poem, evoking storm, shipwreck and the poet-as-shipwrecked-man, framed by gratitude and memory of absent friends. Themes: friendship, the sea, memory.

title: To a Locomotive in Winter
author: Whitman
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Ode addressing a locomotive in a snowstorm as fierce-throated beauty and emblem of modern motion and power, taking the machine as worthy of the Muse.

title: To a President
author: Whitman
summary: A terse rebuke to a president who has not learned the amplitude and impartiality of Nature; free-verse political epigram on the natural order, nation and reform.

title: TO A PRIMROSE
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric to the season's first pale primrose, emblem of timorous hope amid grief and the sweetness of joy following woe; themes of hope, the seasons, and consolation.

title: TO A PROUD PARENT
author: Coleridge
summary: A satirical epigram (after Lessing) implying a child's illegitimacy, since the mother will not teach the infant to call him 'father.'

title: To a Pupil
author: Whitman
summary: Exhortation that reform requires a magnetic Personality of clean body and soul; reform, the body, identity, and self-culture.

title: To a Stranger
author: Whitman
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Address to a passing stranger felt as a long-lost intimate; fleeting urban encounter, recognition, desire, the body and the dream of past shared life.

title: TO A VAIN YOUNG LADY
author: Coleridge
summary: A witty epigram chiding a beautiful woman for vanity, arguing that self-consciousness of her gifts impoverishes her charm; a satire of female pride and self-love.

title: TO A VIRTUOUS OECONOMIST: WERNICKE
author: Coleridge
summary: A complimentary epigram (after Wernicke) praising a frugal man who relieves the needy, hating poverty but not the poor.

title: TO A WELL-KNOWN MUSICAL CRITIC, REMARKABLE FOR HIS EARS STICKING THROUGH HIS HAIR
author: Coleridge
summary: A lampoon on a music critic with protruding ears, invoking the myth of King Midas's ass's ears to ridicule his bad judgment; personal satire drawing on Greek myth.

title: To a Western Boy
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Address to a disciple ('eleve') warning that learning is useless without the blood and silent selection of lovers; comradeship, the body and discipleship.

title: TO A YOUNG ASS: ITS MOTHER BEING TETHERED NEAR IT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Sympathetic address to a foal of an oppressed race, hailing it 'Brother' and longing for a dell of peace and equality; animals, pity, social injustice, pantisocratic ideals.

title: TO A YOUNG FRIEND
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: A blank-verse verse-epistle inviting a young friend to climb an allegorical 'Hill of Knowledge', celebrating retreat into nature, friendship and domestic calm away from worldly fame.

title: TO A YOUNG LADY
author: Coleridge
summary: A light occasional lyric rejoicing at a young lady's recovery from fever, half-jesting that Heaven has angels enough; themes of joy, illness and mortality skirted, with the spring and birds motifs.

title: To a Young Lady who Sent Me a Laurel Crown
author: Keats
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: A sonnet exulting in the laurel crown sent by a lady, defiantly proclaiming poetic ambition above Caesars; the crown of poetic glory and fame.

title: TO A YOUNG LADY WITH A POEM ON THE FRENCH REVOLUTION
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Verse epistle recalling youth and pity, then Freedom bursting her chains and the fall of the Tyrant in France, turning back to a lady and beauty; revolution, liberty, pity, love.

title: TO AN INFANT
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A meditative lyric on an infant grasping for danger, made an emblem of fallen humanity clinging to Faith as nurse of souls; themes of innocence, faith, and human frailty.

title: TO AN UNFORTUNATE WOMAN AT THE THEATRE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Outsider · Fall from Innocence · The (Reputed) Fallen Woman
summary: A lyric addressing a 'fallen' woman seduced and forsaken, urging her toward penitent melancholy and recovered innocence; themes of seduction, the fallen woman and redemptive melancholy.

title: TO AN UNFORTUNATE WOMAN WHOM THE AUTHOR HAD KNOWN IN THE DAYS OF HER INNOCENCE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Outsider · Fall from Innocence · The (Reputed) Fallen Woman
summary: A short lyric figuring a ruined woman as a myrtle-leaf danced from its stalk by a flatterer and left to rot; an allegory of seduction, lost innocence and the fallen woman.

title: TO ASRA
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A love-sonnet to Asra (Sara Hutchinson) whose ever-welling love, likened to spring-waters through snow, the poet would transmute into a dower of happy life and eternity for her.

title: TO AUTUMN
author: Keats
summary: Ode to the season of ripeness and harvest that quietly accepts decline and the coming of death in its music of the soft-dying day; nature, the seasons, transience and serene acceptance of mortality.

title: TO BABY BATES
author: Coleridge
cluster: Maturation and Growth · Childhood · Innocence and Experience
summary: A tender lullaby to an American infant contrasting wealthy Columbia with poor Britain yet affirming all are children of one God of Love; childhood, poverty, and divine love.

title: TO CAPTAIN FINDLAY
author: Coleridge
summary: A jaunty sea-toast saluting a ship's captain who rightly foretold a fair wind, with refrain 'Bravo! Captain Findlay'; conviviality and the sea voyage to Malta.

title: TO CHARLES COWDEN CLARKE
author: Keats
summary: Verse epistle of gratitude to his mentor Clarke for opening to him Spenser, Tasso and the classics; friendship, poetic apprenticeship and the passing of time.

title: TO DISAPPOINTMENT
author: Coleridge
summary: An ode banishing the fiend Disappointment and invoking sweet May to bring peace, health, and filial and maternal joy to the poet's mother in the Welsh vales.

title: TO EARL STANHOPE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: A revised sonnet to Stanhope, casting him as an Abdiel-like faithful champion of Freedom and her God against rebellious nobility; themes of virtue, liberty, and martyred righteousness.

title: TO EDWARD IRVING
author: Coleridge
summary: Verses to the preacher Edward Irving on the divine Reason and Absolute Will, plus a comic Luther-on-devils squib; theological reflection mixed with affectionate wit.

title: To F--
author: Poe
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A love lyric: amid the woes of his earthly path the speaker finds solace in the memory of the beloved, likened to a serene enchanted isle in a stormy sea. Themes of love, consolation and melancholy.

title: TO FORTUNE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Mock-serious ode addressing blindfold Fortune on buying a lottery ticket; gold, hope, poverty and the flower of hope. Satirical occasional lyric.

title: TO FORTUNE
author: Coleridge
summary: Brief prose epistle to the editor introducing the poem 'To Fortune'; a satiric/occasional note framing an address to the goddess Fortune and the lottery.

title: To Frances S. Osgood
author: Poe
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A short complimentary love lyric counselling the beloved to remain exactly as she is to be endlessly praised and loved. Themes of love, beauty and constancy.

title: To G. A. W
author: Keats
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: Sonnet blazon praising the varied loveliness of a woman in her moods and graceful movement; romantic admiration of feminine beauty.

title: TO GEORGE FELTON MATHEW
author: Keats
summary: Verse epistle on the brotherhood of poets, lamenting the dark city that stifles the muse and longing for poetic fellowship and nature; friendship and the poet's vocation.

title: To Get the Final Lilt of Songs
author: Whitman
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: To fully grasp the great poets one needs old age and the experience it brings as the final faculty.

title: To Haydon
author: Keats
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: A sonnet to the painter Haydon, professing the poet's inadequacy before mighty art and praising Haydon's vision against the dull crowd; the artist, genius and aspiration.

title: To Helen
author: Poe
summary: A longer blank-verse love lyric recalling a single moonlit vision of Helen in an enchanted rose-garden, whose haunting eyes guide and enslave the speaker ever after. Themes of idealized love, beauty, eyes and memory.

title: To Helen
author: Poe
summary: Poe's classic lyric praising Helen's beauty as a Nicean bark bearing the wanderer home to 'the glory that was Greece, and the grandeur that was Rome'. Themes of beauty, idealized love and classical antiquity.

title: To Him That Was Crucified
author: Whitman
cluster: Martyrdom · The Martyr / Saint · The Cross
summary: Address to Christ as a fellow comrade and equal labourer transmitting the same charge across all lands and creeds; the Christ figure, comradeship, and universal brotherhood.

title: TO HOPE
author: Keats
summary: Personified ode to Hope as comforter against despondency and despair, ending in a patriotic prayer for England's liberty; melancholy answered by hope.

title: To Isadore
author: Poe
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A musical love lyric celebrating Isadore as a dream-enchantress whose voice and violet eyes wake old memories and turn the speaker's name to melody. Themes of idealized love, beauty, dreams and memory.

title: TO KOSCIUSKO
author: Keats
summary: Sonnet hymning the Polish patriot-hero Kosciusko, joining his name with Alfred's as everlasting heroic music; heroism, liberty and the immortality of great names.

title: TO LESBIA
author: Coleridge
summary: Imitation of Catullus's 'Vivamus mea Lesbia': carpe-diem invitation to love and count kisses, contrasting the recurring sun with humans' endless night of death.

title: TO LORD STANHOPE
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: A sonnet hailing Stanhope as an incorruptible 'Friend of Humankind' pleading the cause of Nature and Liberty; themes of patriotism, virtue, and freedom.

title: To Marie Louise (shew)
author: Poe
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A grateful blank-verse tribute to Marie Louise Shew, whose presence restores the despairing speaker's faith in Truth, Virtue and Humanity, her words echoing the divine 'Let there be light'. Themes of love, gratitude, faith and the angelic beloved.

title: TO MARY PRIDHAM
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A father's blessing on his son Derwent's betrothed, reviving the poet's hope at the fulfilment of a son's earliest wish in love. Themes: romantic/familial love, hope, fulfilment.

title: TO MATILDA BETHAM FROM A STRANGER
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Verse-epistle praising a young poetess and urging bold yet truth-rooted art, linking female mind to music and to patriotic hope. Themes of art, nature, and the poet's vocation.

title: TO MISS BRUNTON
author: Coleridge
summary: Compliment to actress Miss Brunton via Thalia and the Tragic/Comic Muses; light lyric on the artist, beauty and the Muses of drama.

title: TO MR. PYE
author: Coleridge
summary: A literary-satirical epigram mocking the Laureate Pye's 'Carmen Seculare' as eternal because incomprehensible and 'without head or tail.'

title: TO MY BROTHER GEORGE
author: Keats
summary: Sonnet on the wonders of sea and sky witnessed in a day, made meaningful only by the absent brother's shared thought; nature, the sea and fraternal love.

title: TO MY BROTHER GEORGE
author: Keats
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: Verse epistle on poetic doubt and inspiration: the trance of the poet who sees visionary knights in the clouds, hopes for poetic immortality, and treasures fraternal love.

title: TO MY BROTHERS
author: Keats
summary: Domestic sonnet for Tom's birthday by the fireside, quietly aware that the 'great voice' of death will one day part the brothers; fraternal love and mortality.

title: TO MY CANDLE
author: Coleridge
summary: A 'farewell epigram' addressed to a candle, whose short pointed flame is itself an image of the epigram; a self-reflexive meditation on light, brevity, and the art of the epigram.

title: TO NATURE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: A sonnet making nature itself a temple: the poet builds an altar in the fields and worships God through leaves and flowers. Themes: nature as worship, piety, the book of nature.

title: To One in Paradise
author: Poe
summary: An elegiac love lyric mourning a dead beloved who was the speaker's whole hope; the light of life is now over, his days mere trances. Themes of grief, lost love, mortality and despair.

title: To One Shortly to Die
author: Whitman
summary: Tender address to a dying person, telling them merciless truth yet congratulating their spiritual escape; the corpse is mere excrement, the soul eternal.

title: TO ONE WHO HAS BEEN LONG IN CITY PENT
author: Keats
cluster: Nature vs Civilization · The Garden · Pastoral Retreat
summary: Sonnet on the sweetness of escaping the city into open countryside to read of love; nature versus the city, transience of the happy day.

title: TO ONE WHO PUBLISHED IN PRINT
author: Coleridge
summary: A cluster of satirical epigrams (several adapted from Wernicke) attacking a treacherous friend, the spread of scandal and lies, and a sneering miser; themes of betrayed friendship, falsehood, and avarice.

title: To Rich Givers
author: Whitman
summary: The poet cheerfully accepts modest gifts as he rendezvous with his poems, giving in return the entrance to all the gifts of the universe; free-verse on the open road, the poet and gift.

title: TO RICHARD BRINSLEY SHERIDAN, ESQ.
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet praising Sheridan's eloquence and wit, ranging from Petrarchan sweetness to patriot rage that scorches the political apostate; themes of eloquence, satire, and patriotism.

title: TO SIMPLICITY
author: Coleridge
summary: A parodic sonnet satirising the cult of affected 'simplicity' and self-pitying melancholy in contemporary poetry; a satire of poetic fashion in sonnet form.

title: TO SOME LADIES
author: Keats
summary: Light occasional lyric thanking ladies for a sea-shell keepsake; nature, friendship and graceful compliment in moon-lit pastoral imagery.

title: to st michael
author: Chesterton
summary: A martial hymn invoking the Archangel Michael, who threw down the Dragon, to guard the Word against the soft corruptions of a false peace bought with gold and bribes.

title: TO SUSAN STEELE ON RECEIVING THE PURSE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Comic 'extrumpery' lines thanking Susan for a purse the poet has no cash to fill, joking about lost money and a kiss for the purse; light verse on poverty and money.

title: TO T. POOLE: AN INVITATION
author: Coleridge
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: A boisterous comic dinner invitation in dialect promising meat, potatoes and cabbage and mock-cursing the friend if he stays away; conviviality, feasting, and friendship.

title: TO THE AUTHOR OF POEMS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: A verse epistle to Joseph Cottle praising his modest verse via an allegory of the Poetic mount, Oblivion's stream, and the impassioned theme Poesy demands; themes of poetry, the artist, and nature.

title: TO THE AUTHOR OF ‘THE ROBBERS’
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Sonnet to Schiller in awe of the terror and sublimity of his tragedy; the sublime, terror and horror, the artist, and a Gothic dungeon scene.

title: To the East and to the West
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Address across the regions of the States proclaiming a 'superb friendship' latent in all men; comradeship as the purpose of the nation, democracy.

title: TO THE EVENING STAR
author: Coleridge
summary: An apostrophe sonnet hailing the evening star as an emblem of the beloved's serene beauty and of a hope to join her spirit in its kindred orb.

title: To the Garden the World
author: Whitman
summary: Opening of Children of Adam: speaker as new Adam re-ascending to the garden with Eve, celebrating the body and resurrection through love; Edenic, sexual, cyclic.

title: TO THE HONOURABLE MR. ERSKINE
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet from the 'Sonnets on Eminent Characters' praising Erskine as a 'hireless Priest' defending British Freedom with eloquence; themes of liberty, fame surviving the tomb, and the poet's immortalizing power.

title: To the Indians who Died in Africa
author: Eliot
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: WWII elegy for Indian soldiers who died fighting in Africa; meditates on death, home, exile and the fruit of action known only after the judgment.

title: To the Ladies who Saw Me Crown’d
author: Keats
summary: A sonnet weighing the bay wreath against natural beauties and finally bowing to the ladies' sovereign eyes; poetic glory, beauty and gallant compliment.

title: To the Leaven’d Soil They Trod
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: Closing Drum-Taps benediction to the American land that witnessed war and peace, the soil and continent nourishing and ripening the poet's songs.

title: To the Man-of-War-Bird
author: Whitman
summary: An apostrophe to the storm-riding frigate-bird as emblem of soul and freedom over sea and sky; free-verse lyric on birds, the sea, storm and the soul.

title: TO THE MUSE
author: Coleridge
cluster: Imagination · Creativity and Artistic Labor · The One Life (Pantheism)
summary: A lyric thanking the Muse for refining the poet's soul, softening sorrow into joy, and teaching pity and gentle satire of fashion and folly.

title: TO THE NIGHTINGALE
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric addressing the nightingale (Philomel), 'most musical, most melancholy', yet finding the beloved Sara's voice sweeter; themes of poetic melancholy, love, and the bird as symbol.

title: To the Pending Year
author: Whitman
summary: A fierce, self-interrogating address to the coming year, the poet searching for a last weapon-word against affectation and his own rebellious self.

title: TO THE REV. GEORGE COLERIDGE
author: Coleridge
summary: A prose dedicatory letter to the poet's brother arguing that mathematics, the quintessence of truth, starves the imagination, and proposing to wed Mathesis to poetic Harmony.

title: TO THE REV. GEORGE COLERIDGE OF OTTERY ST. MARY, DEVON
author: Coleridge
summary: A blank-verse epistle to his brother contrasting George's settled domestic happiness with the poet's restless wandering and alienation; themes of friendship, exile, home and providence.

title: TO THE REV. W. J. HORT: WHILE TEACHING A YOUNG LADY SOME SONG-TUNES ON HIS FLUTE
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric on flute-music waking memory and hope and dreams of retirement with the beloved in Freedom's dell; themes of music, love, and rural retreat.

title: TO THE REV. W. L. BOWLES
author: Coleridge
summary: A sonnet of grateful tribute to the poet Bowles, whose tender verse healed the speaker's melancholy youth; themes of poetry's consolation, sympathy, and the imagination.

title: To the River--
author: Poe
summary: A short love lyric making the clear river an emblem of the beloved's beauty and unhidden heart, her image deep in the speaker's trembling heart. Themes of love, beauty, water and reflection.

title: To the States
author: Whitman
summary: Aphoristic political lyric: resist much, obey little; warns against enslavement and loss of liberty. Democracy, the rebel, reform.

title: To The States (To Identify the 16th, 17th, or 18th Presidentiad)
author: Whitman
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: A political lyric of disgust at corrupt antebellum government, prophesying that the sleeping States will awake; a satire of political decay and a call to democratic vigilance.

title: To the Sun-Set Breeze
author: Whitman
cluster: Nature · The Book of Nature · The Natural Order
summary: The sick, aged poet addresses the cooling evening wind through his window as a spiritual, God-sent messenger linking him to nature and the cosmos.

title: TO THE YOUNG ARTIST: KAYSER OF KASERWERTH
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A complimentary verse-letter to a young portrait artist, praising his genius and skill at making the absent present through art.

title: To Thee Old Cause
author: Whitman
summary: Dedication to the deathless cause of liberty for which all wars are fought; the wheel-on-axis image; war, democracy, eternal struggle. Free verse.

title: To Think of Time
author: Whitman
summary: Extended meditation on mortality, burial and time that concludes in defiant affirmation of the eternal soul and universal immortality.

title: To Those Who’ve Fail’d
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse tribute raising a laurel monument to those cut off by early death before their aspirations were realized; themes of failure, death and heroism.

title: TO TWO SISTERS: (MARY MORGAN AND CHARLOTTE BRENT)
author: Coleridge
summary: A Wanderer's Farewell thanking two sisters whose kindness recalled his beloved sisters, blending memory, grief and despairing hope. Themes of love, grief, memory and the wanderer's loneliness.

title: To Walter de la Mare
author: Eliot
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Tribute poem in terza rima praising de la Mare's art of evoking the supernatural, ghosts, dreams and the uncanny through sound and craft.

title: TO WILLIAM GODWIN
author: Coleridge
cluster: Justice / Right and Wrong · Revenge · Avenger
summary: A sonnet to the author of 'Political Justice', hailing his enlightening reason against oppression; themes of justice, reform, and intellectual liberation.

title: TO WILLIAM WORDSWORTH COMPOSED ON THE NIGHT AFTER HIS RECITATION OF A POEM ON THE GROWTH OF AN INDIVIDUAL MIND
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: Major blank-verse tribute to Wordsworth's recitation of The Prelude, on the growth of mind, hope born of the French Revolution, and the poet's own grief and reawakening. Themes of imagination, memory, the poet as prophet and dejection turning to prayer.

title: To You
author: Whitman
summary: A direct free-verse address to the unknown reader, affirming the divine worth, identity and unrealized soul of every person; democratic intimacy and the self.

title: To Zante
author: Poe
summary: A sonnet on the Greek isle of Zante, whose flowery shores now wake only memories of a vanished maiden and entombed hopes; the place is cursed by the refrain 'no more'. Themes of grief, lost love, transience and the classical Mediterranean.

title: To —
author: Keats
summary: A tender consolatory lyric urging a weeping beloved not to grieve over a fleeting bliss, proposing a dirge of kisses; transience, love, grief and consolation.

title: to-belloc
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Road · Napoleonic Wars / the Navy
summary: A dedicatory lyric to Belloc (preface to The Napoleon of Notting Hill), dreaming an epic hour of revolution and battle where streets of earth meet the starry streets that point to God.

title: To-Day and Thee
author: Whitman
summary: The whole heirdom of human history and art converges in the present 'thee', a meditation on time and inheritance.

title: to-frances
author: Chesterton
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Whimsical love-letters and a mock-autobiography addressed to his fiancee Frances Blogg; turns ordinary domestic objects sacramental, treats love and death as kindred transformations.

title: tolstoy
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A critical essay (with Perris and Garnett) on Tolstoy: his cult of simplification, his realism about war, and Chesterton's argument that logic without mysticism breeds fanaticism and madness.

title: towers-of-time
author: Chesterton
summary: A visionary lyric on the mutability and fall of empires, thrones and republics, set against the eternal endurance of the Virgin and the City of God outlasting all towers men rear.

title: Translation from a Sonnet of Ronsard
author: Keats
summary: A translated sonnet on the heavenly-made beauty of Cassandra, whose descent sets the poet's heart afire with sweet burning pain. It treats idealized beauty, romantic love, and Greek myth.

title: TRANSLATION OF A FRAGMENT OF HERACLITUS
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: A verse rendering of Heraclitus on the Sibyl's prophetic voice rolling unadorned truth through a thousand years, plus a couplet on truth and erring fancy.

title: TRANSLATION OF A LATIN INSCRIPTION BY THE REV. W. L. BOWLES IN NETHER-STOWEY CHURCH
author: Coleridge
summary: A short translated funerary epitaph bidding a departed parent go in joy from the world's strife to celestial quiet; themes of mortality, grief, faith and consolation.

title: TRANSLATION OF A PASSAGE IN OTTFRIED’S METRICAL PARAPHRASE OF THE GOSPEL
author: Coleridge
summary: A devotional translation celebrating the Virgin Mother nursing the infant Christ, blending natural maternal imagery with religious mystery and litany-like blessing.

title: TRANSLATION OF THE FIRST STROPHE OF PINDAR’S SECOND OLYMPIC
author: Coleridge
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: A literal English version of the opening strophe of Pindar's Second Olympic ode (celebrating victor and city) plus a fragment on superstition as the shadow of weak mortality.

title: TRANSLATION OF WRANGHAM’S ‘HENDECASYLLABI AD BRUNTONAM E GRANTA EXITURAM’ (KAL. OCT.MDCCXC)
author: Coleridge
summary: Tribute to the actress Miss Brunton, praising her truth, pity and tragic art (Monimia, Juliet, Euphrasia); art, beauty, theatrical sorrow and Pierian garlands.

title: Transpositions
author: Whitman
summary: Epigrammatic world-upside-down poem reversing judges and criminals, keepers and prisoners; satirical reformist inversion of social order.

title: trees of pride
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A 1922 mystery novella set on the Cornish coast: peasant legends of poisonous 'peacock trees', a squire's disappearance, a faked murder unravelled by a detective doctor; pits rational scepticism against folk wisdom.

title: Tremendous Trifles
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A 1909 collection of familiar essays finding the marvellous in commonplace objects and events; teaches wonder, gratitude and the renewing of perception against habitual blindness.

title: Tribute To Gladstone
author: Chesterton
summary: An 1898 elegiac tribute on Gladstone's death, celebrating a strong man who died with his head high and rebuking the grey, sad spirit of the decadent younger generation.

title: Trickle Drops
author: Whitman
cluster: Letters and Writing · Immortality Through Verse · Immortality of Art / Fame
summary: Intense Calamus lyric in which 'confession drops' of blood stain every page; blood, confession, shame and the body as the bleeding source of song.

title: TROCHAICS
author: Coleridge
summary: A trochaic metrical experiment on a diviner spirit and unearthly sound making heroic hearts faint; prosodic study with visionary, supernatural imagery.

title: TROILUS AND CRESSIDA
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Disillusionment · Odysseus / Ulysses · Grace Under Pressure / Stoic Endurance
summary: A bitter, philosophical play set during the Trojan War that deflates heroic ideals and dramatizes the betrayal of love by Cressida; a sardonic anatomy of war, lust, time and the frailty of human value.

title: True Conquerors
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: Old workers, sailors and soldiers who merely survived their struggles are the true conquerors over all the rest.

title: Turn O Libertad
author: Whitman
cluster: The French Revolution · Liberty / Political Freedom · Pindaric Ode
summary: Post-war summons to Liberty to turn from the feudal past of kings and slavery toward a democratic future; patriotism, progress, and the rejection of the old order.

title: turnpikes
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A 1933 familiar essay defending the maligned 'medieval' against the cult of modernity, using a turnpike-toll to expose the worship of speed and progress; paradoxical social criticism.

title: TWELFTH NIGHT
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A festive romantic comedy of shipwreck, twins, cross-dressing disguise and mistaken identity in Illyria, where tangled love, music and folly resolve in marriage; a comedy turning on appearance versus reality.

title: Twelve Types
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A 1902 collection of critical-biographical essays on figures such as Bronte, Byron, Pope, St Francis, Carlyle, Tolstoy, Savonarola and Scott; literary criticism probing each subject's character and ideals.

title: twelve-men
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: An essay on jury service arguing that the ordinary man, not the expert, must judge grave human matters; defends the common man, tragedy as the value of life, and Christian wisdom.

title: Twenty Years
author: Whitman
summary: A sailor returns after twenty years circling the globe to find the place changed and parents dead; a meditation on time and homecoming.

title: Two Kinds of Paradox
author: Chesterton
summary: A 1911 essay distinguishing fruitful, life-giving paradox (Lear, Carroll) from barren, thought-killing epigram (Shaw, Nietzsche imitators); a meditation on nonsense, art and truth.

title: Two or Three
author: Keats
summary: A playful nonsense-verse jingle from a letter to his sister, built on the refrain 'two or three' and ending self-referentially on hatching sonnets; light comic song.

title: Ulalume
author: Poe
summary: An incantatory, hauntingly musical ballad: the speaker, wandering a ghoul-haunted October woodland with his Soul (Psyche), is led to the tomb of his lost beloved Ulalume, exactly a year after burying her. Themes of grief, death, memory and the supernatural night-journey.

title: unborn
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: A lyric poem spoken by an unborn child longing to enter the world; its central themes are wonder and gratitude for existence, innocence before experience, and the magic of ordinary life seen as fairyland.

title: UNDERWOODS
author: Coleridge
summary: Ben Jonson's 'The Hour-Glass': the dust in the glass is the burnt body of a dead lover, so that even lovers' ashes find no rest; a conceit on time, death and love.

title: UNFINISHED POEMS
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: Section file containing Sweeney Agonistes: jazz-rhythm verse drama of birth/copulation/death, murder, dread; spiritual emptiness of the modern waste land.

title: Unfolded out of the Folds
author: Whitman
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: Litany that man and all his greatness is unfolded out of woman; the great mother, the body, and the generative origin of poems and justice.

title: United States
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A biographical memoir-preface honouring his brother Cecil, tracing his conversion to Catholicism and Distributism, his exposure of the Marconi corruption, and his death in the First World War fighting Prussianism.

title: unity
author: Chesterton
summary: A satirical ballad about a missionary literally devoured by converts, mocking the modern doctrine of religious syncretism and forced unity of faiths; combines comic verse with theological satire.

title: unknown-warrior
author: Chesterton
summary: A lyric poem celebrating the anonymous dead soldier whose nameless heroism defeats vulgar publicity and commercial fame; central themes are war's cost, honour, and the dignity of the unknown.

title: Unnamed Land
author: Whitman
summary: On the countless vanished nations and unrecorded dead who nonetheless still exist; ubi sunt, mortality, immortality of the soul, and memory.

title: Unseen Buds
author: Whitman
summary: Hidden under snow and ice, infinite germinal buds wait latent throughout earth and cosmos, urging slowly forward in endless unborn becoming.

title: upon-this-rock
author: Chesterton
summary: An apologetics essay expounding Roman Catholicism: the Papacy, the Eucharist, Penance, asceticism, and the cult of the Virgin, defending the Church as guardian of faith against heresies.

title: UtopiaUsurers
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A collection of polemical essays attacking capitalism, plutocracy, and the Servile State, advocating Distributism and warning of a dystopia ruled by usurers; opens with militant verse on the Irish road.

title: V If the lost word is lost, if the spent word is spent
author: Eliot
cluster: Grace and Redemption · Humility · The Desert
summary: Meditation on the silent unspoken Word (Logos) shining in darkness amid a noisy world, with the Reproaches 'O my people'; the Word, silence, grace, the desert/garden and prayer of the veiled sister.

title: V O Lord, deliver me from the man of excellent intention and impure heart
author: Eliot
summary: Prayer against the deceitful heart amid snakes and dogs; humility, purity, silence, conscience; sin and the watchful labour of faith.

title: V, W, X
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: Index-of-first-lines fragment (V–X) listing openings such as 'We are the hollow men', 'Webster was much possessed by death' and 'When Mr. Apollinax visited the United States'; apparatus to the corpus.

title: V. What the Thunder said
author: Eliot
cluster: Spiritual Emptiness · Eastern Religion / Comparative Religion · Self and Cosmos
summary: Final section: the waterless rock journey, the hooded figure on the road to Emmaus, the empty chapel, falling cities and the thunder's Datta/Dayadhvam/Damyata; quest, redemption sought, drought and fragments shored against ruin.

title: VariedTypes
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A collection of critical essays on figures such as Charlotte Bronte, William Morris, Byron, Pope, St Francis, Stevenson, Carlyle and Tolstoy; literary criticism that probes the inner truth and creed behind each writer's art.

title: VARIOUS POEMS
author: Shakespeare
summary: A miscellany of short poems attributed to Shakespeare (songs, Passionate Pilgrim pieces, the metaphysical elegy 'The Phoenix and Turtle', and epitaphs) ranging over love, beauty's transience, constancy and mortality.

title: vegetarian
author: Chesterton
cluster: Wine and Drink · Food and Feasting · The Inn / Tavern
summary: A comic nonsense song (from The Flying Inn) mocking faddish vegetarianism and abstract logic through a drunkard who calls himself a rigid vegetarian; light satire built on wine, the inn, and paradox.

title: VENUS AND ADONIS
author: Shakespeare
cluster: Lust / Sexual Desire · Desire · Sin and the Fall
summary: Ovidian erotic narrative poem in sixains: the goddess Venus's failed seduction of the chaste youth Adonis, who is killed by a boar. Central themes: desire and lust, the unattainable beloved, beauty, mortality and transience.

title: VER PERPETUUM
author: Coleridge
summary: A short fragment on transient mortals hoping for a brighter destiny of one perpetual Spring; themes of transience, hope, and immortality.

title: Vera, or The Nihilists
author: Wilde
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: Wilde's first play, a melodramatic political tragedy set in Tsarist Russia about nihilist revolutionaries plotting to assassinate the Czar; Vera's sworn oath to renounce love and pity collides with her love for the Czarevitch, ending in self-sacrifice. Central themes: tyranny and revolution, love versus duty, oath and betrayal, martyrdom.

title: VERSES: ADDRESSED TO J. HORNE TOOKE AND THE COMPANY WHO MET ON JUNE 28TH, 1796,
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A political celebratory poem hailing Horne Tooke and the dawn of Freedom against Corruption, citing his persecution and Roman tyrannicide; themes of liberty, reform, and political injustice.

title: VERSES TRIVOCULAR
author: Coleridge
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A nonsense jeu d'esprit built on a chain of '-ocular' rhymes about unilocular hearts, roquelaures and periwinkles; comic verbal play and wit for its own sake.

title: VI Although I do not hope to turn again
author: Eliot
summary: Closing section of Ash-Wednesday: penitential prayer poised between birth and dying, sea imagery, surrender to God's will. Religious conversion and faith-doubt tension.

title: VI It is hard for those who have never known persecution
author: Eliot
summary: Chorus on complacent comfort and persecution, why men should love the Church which speaks of Evil and Sin; faith, doubt, sin, satire of society.

title: Victorian Age
author: Chesterton
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: A book-length critical survey of Victorian literature, treating the Victorian Compromise, its great novelists and poets, and the breakup of that compromise; argues that a writer's creed and moral attitude are inseparable from his art.

title: Vigil Strange I Kept on the Field One Night
author: Whitman
summary: A soldier keeps an all-night vigil over the body of a fallen comrade-son and buries him at dawn; an elegy of comradeship, death and love.

title: VII In the beginning god created the world
author: Eliot
summary: History of religion from Genesis chaos to the Incarnation, a moment in and out of time; faith, the bible, light and dark, the ages of the world.

title: VIII O Father we welcome your words
author: Eliot
summary: Chorus on the Crusades and Peter the Hermit, mixed motives of glory, greed and faith; the bible, the Crusades, faith, martyrdom and moral corruption.

title: Villette
author: Bronte
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Charlotte Bronte's first-person psychological bildungsroman: the isolated Lucy Snowe teaches at Mme Beck's school in the foreign city of Villette, enduring repression, surveillance, unrequited love and the spectral nun. Central themes are loneliness, self-suppression, Protestant/Catholic conflict and the ambiguous, storm-shadowed close.

title: Virginia--The West
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: An allegory in which the rebellious South lifts a knife against the Mother of All while the loyal West (drest in blue) rushes to her rescue; the Union defended.

title: Vocalism
author: Whitman
summary: On the hard-won divine power to speak words and the magnetic right voice that all things obey; the body, the artist, identity, and song.

title: Von Kempelen and his Discovery
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A pseudo-scientific hoax-tale presenting Von Kempelen's alchemical discovery of turning lead into gold and its economic consequences. Themes of gold, science, satire and appearance vs reality.

title: W. L. BOWLES
author: Coleridge
summary: A meditative lyric (1793) in the manner of Bowles, mourning misspent youth and longing that all who silently mourn might hear joy, accepting man's mixed lot of pleasure, toil and pain by God's will.

title: Wandering at Morn
author: Whitman
summary: Morning meditation in which a singing thrush, transmuting grubs and worms into song, becomes a hopeful emblem for the troubled Union's future.

title: Warble for Lilac-Time
author: Whitman
summary: Joyous spring catalog of returning lilac-time and birds rousing the restless soul to fly forth; spring, flowers, birds, nature, and the soul's longing.

title: Washington’s Monument February, 1885
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: Washington's true monument is not marble but the worldwide spirit of freedom, courage and patriotism.

title: WATER BALLAD
author: Coleridge
summary: A song translated from the French in which a river-crossing becomes a courtship; the boat becomes the lovers' home, blending the journey-over-water with love and marriage.

title: We Two Boys Together Clinging
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Exuberant catalogue of two inseparable comrades roaming, mocking statutes and owning no law but themselves; comradeship, the open road, rebellion and the body.

title: We Two, How Long We Were Fool’d
author: Whitman
summary: Two lovers transmuted into all of nature, returning home to freedom and joy; love, nature, eternal return, cosmic identity.

title: Weave in, My Hardy Life
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: A free-verse lyric using the weaving metaphor to urge ceaseless labor of life in campaigns of peace and war; themes of the soldier, work and life-as-struggle.

title: Well And Shallows
author: Chesterton
summary: A late collection of controversial Catholic essays (1935) defending the Church against modern materialism, sex reform, and the Reformation legacy; argues conversion is a return to the deep well of tradition rather than the modern shallows.

title: WESTPHALIAN SONG
author: Coleridge
cluster: Romantic Love · The Lover · Unrequited / Frustrated Love
summary: A literal translation of a Westphalian folk-song, a wry lover's message turning on a feigned report of death and a promise of return tomorrow.

title: What Am I After All
author: Whitman
summary: Tiny lyric on the self as a child pleased with the sound of its own name; identity, the self, childhood, and language.

title: What Best I See in Thee
author: Whitman
summary: A free-verse tribute to U. S. Grant whose real greatness lies in carrying the common Western people with him among kings; themes of the common man and democracy.

title: WHAT IS LIFE?
author: Coleridge
summary: Philosophical riddle-poem questioning the nature of life as a war-embrace of life and death and of consciousness. Metaphysical meditation on existence and mortality.

title: What is Right With the World
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A philosophical essay arguing that existence is fundamentally good at its origin (not merely at some progressive end), attacking facile optimism, Meliorism, and the modern cult of unity; celebrates wonder, variety and the dignity of the common life.

title: What Place Is Besieged?
author: Whitman
cluster: Swords and Weapons · The Battlefield · Horse
summary: Brief martial allegory: to a besieged place the poet sends an immortal commander with artillery; war imagery, the poet-hero, weapons.

title: What Ship Puzzled at Sea
author: Whitman
summary: Quatrain offering the soul, as a perfect pilot rowing out in a little boat, to guide the puzzled ship of the self into the true channel.

title: What the Thrush Said
author: Keats
summary: An unrhymed sonnet-letter spoken as the thrush's counsel, urging trust in instinctive song over anxious pursuit of knowledge, set against winter passing into spring. Central to it are negative capability, the seasons, and the value of receptive idleness.

title: What Think You I Take My Pen in Hand?
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Poet records not the battle-ship or great city but two men kissing in parting on a pier; comradely love privileged over public grandeur.

title: WhatISawInAmerica
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A book of travel essays reflecting on American democracy, Prohibition, business, Lincoln and the spirit of the nation; meditates on the rights of man, the creed of equality, and the contrast between America and England.

title: whats wrong
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Chesterton's 1910 book-length work of social criticism arguing that modern society misdiagnoses its ills; it defends the family, property and tradition against industrialism, imperialism, feminism and mechanical schooling, and advances his distributist programme.

title: When I Heard at the Close of the Day
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Calamus poem contrasting empty public fame with the happiness of lying beside the sleeping beloved by the sea; love, the body, the sea, dawn and autumn imagery.

title: When I Heard the Learn’d Astronomer
author: Whitman
summary: Wearied by the lecturer's charts, the poet wanders out to look in silence at the stars; a free-verse lyric contrasting dry science with mystical wonder, on stars, night and nature.

title: When I Peruse the Conquer’d Fame
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Poet envies not generals or presidents but the 'brotherhood of lovers'; comradeship and faithful love exalted over heroism and worldly fame.

title: When I Read the Book
author: Whitman
summary: Skeptical lyric on the impossibility of biography truly knowing a life, including one's own; identity, memory, the book and writing.

title: When Lilacs Last in the Dooryard Bloom’d
author: Whitman
summary: Whitman's great pastoral elegy for the assassinated Lincoln, built on the trinity of lilac, fallen western star, and hermit thrush, culminating in a hymn of reconciliation to 'lovely and soothing death.'

title: When the Full-Grown Poet Came
author: Whitman
cluster: The Poet as Prophet · The Great Mother · The Prophet
summary: An ars-poetica parable of the poet as reconciler standing between Nature and the Soul of man, joining their hands and blending them into one.

title: While Not the Past Forgetting
author: Whitman
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: Reconciliation poem laying wreaths on the graves of all dead soldiers, North and South, for peace and brotherhood.

title: Whispers of Heavenly Death
author: Whitman
summary: Hushed nocturnal lyric in which murmurs, unseen rivers and a dimmed star intimate a soul passing over as a solemn immortal birth.

title: Whispers of Immortality
author: Eliot
summary: Quatrain poem setting Webster and Donne's metaphysical obsession with death and the skull against the fleshly modern Grishkin; mortality, the body, desire and metaphysical wit.

title: white-horse2
author: Chesterton
cluster: Swords and Weapons · The Battlefield · Horse
summary: Chesterton's long narrative ballad-epic on King Alfred's stand against the heathen Danes at Ethandune, framed as legend rather than history; it celebrates Christian civilization, hope against odds, and the last stand of the West.

title: Who Learns My Lesson Complete?
author: Whitman
cluster: Wonder and Gratitude · The Sublime · Sun
summary: Free-verse catalogue addressing all classes of people; meditates on the wonder of the cosmos and the speaker's own immortality, finding ordinary existence equally marvelous.

title: Whoever You Are Holding Me Now in Hand
author: Whitman
cluster: Comradeship · The Open Road / Homecoming · The Union
summary: Calamus opening poem warning the reader-lover about the cost of comradely love; free-verse meditation on intimacy, elusive identity, and the demanding 'novitiate' of love between comrades.

title: WhoGoesHome
author: Chesterton
cluster: War and its Cost · Blood · American Civil War
summary: A short, martial lyric on the city, parliament and the call 'Who goes home?', turning a civic cry into a meditation on blood, liberty, victory and the soul's homecoming after death.

title: Why the Little Frenchman Wears his Hand in a Sling
author: Poe
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A broad dialect comedy narrated in thick Irish brogue by a vain 'Barronitt' courting a widow, who is duped in a hand-holding ruse with a French rival. Themes of farcical satire, vanity and deception.

title: wifrb11
author: Chesterton
cluster: Appearance vs Reality · Deception · Short Story
summary: A collection of detective short stories in which the unassuming priest Father Brown solves crimes through moral and psychological insight rather than science, exploring appearance versus reality, sin, and the human heart.

title: Wild Ducks
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: A posthumous collection of Chesterton's journalistic essays on manners, culture, civilization, travel and everyday wonders; paradoxical, satirical prose celebrating the common life and gratitude while criticizing modern society and progress.

title: William Cobbett
author: Chesterton
cluster: Essay · Critique of Progress · The Common Man
summary: Chesterton's critical biography of the radical pamphleteer and rural reformer William Cobbett, championing him as a self-made patriot and prophet of the common Englishman against industrialism, and a forerunner of distributist ideals.

title: William Wilson
author: Poe
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: A doppelganger tale: the dissolute narrator is shadowed all his life by a double bearing his own name who thwarts his every vice, until he kills him and destroys himself; the double is his conscience. Themes of the double, conscience, guilt and identity.

title: With All Thy Gifts
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: Apostrophe to a powerful, wealthy America asking whether it lacks the one gift of perfect women and mothers fit for it.

title: With Antecedents
author: Whitman
summary: The present America as the heir and centre of all past ages and civilizations; free-verse on history, time, the common man and self as the meeting point of past and future.

title: WITH FIELDING’S ‘AMELIA’
author: Coleridge
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A complimentary sonnet presented with Fielding's novel Amelia, praising its portrayal of wifely and social virtue and wishing a mother's daughters to resemble Amelia.

title: With Husky-Haughty Lips, O Sea!
author: Whitman
summary: Apostrophe to the sea as a chained, striving kindred soul telling the cosmic tale of elemental passion.

title: WORK WITHOUT HOPE
author: Coleridge
