summary: A sonnet contrasting busy springtime Nature with the poet, 'the sole unbusy thing', concluding that work without hope draws nectar in a sieve. Themes: despair, creative sterility, transience, melancholy.

title: World Take Good Notice
author: Whitman
cluster: Nationalism and Patriotism · The First World War · Flags and Banners
summary: A compressed emblem-lyric of the national flag (thirty-eight stars, scarlet stripes) flaunting a warning to the world; patriotic emblem of the Union and the flag.

title: WRITTEN AFTER A WALK BEFORE SUPPER
author: Coleridge
summary: A comic verse-epistle searching for a simile to describe a grotesquely mismatched fat wife and thin husband, settling on an ape chained to a she-bear.

title: WRITTEN IN AN ALBUM
author: Coleridge
summary: A self-deprecating album epigram comparing Parry's polar quest to the poet's quest for rhymes, joking that the public little knows and the publisher knows too much of his works; satire of authorship.

title: WRITTEN ON THE DAY THAT MR. LEIGH HUNT LEFT PRISON
author: Keats
summary: Political sonnet celebrating the imprisoned Leigh Hunt's freedom of spirit (roaming with Spenser and Milton); liberty, friendship and the immortality of genius.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Bronte
cluster: The Supernatural · Terror and Horror · Guilt
summary: Emily Bronte's frame-narrated Gothic novel of the destructive passion between Catherine Earnshaw and the outcast Heathcliff on the Yorkshire moors. Central themes are obsessive love, revenge, social outsiderhood, the supernatural and the bond between the living and the dead.

title: X You have seen the house built, you have seen it adorned
author: Eliot
summary: Closing chorus: the dedicated church as light on a hill, the great snake/serpent of iniquity, the hymn 'O Light Invisible'; faith, light, good vs evil.

title: X-Ing a Paragrab
author: Poe
summary: A comic literary squib: a feud between rival newspaper editors over the letter 'o' ends with a typesetter X-ing out a vowel-laden paragraph into nonsense. Themes of satire of letters, language and folly.

title: Y, Z
author: Eliot
cluster: The Artist and Society · The Book / Reading · Clothing and Costume
summary: Index tail (Y–Z) with Practical Cats lines plus a short biographical note on T. S. Eliot (1888–1965, Nobel 1948); index apparatus and brief author biography.

title: Year of Meteors (1859-60
author: Whitman
summary: A retrospective chant of a portentous year — John Brown's execution, ships, comets and meteors — the poet himself a transient meteor; free-verse on history, mortality and the nation.

title: Year That Trembled and Reel’d Beneath Me
author: Whitman
cluster: Disillusionment · Odysseus / Ulysses · Grace Under Pressure / Stoic Endurance
summary: A brief lyric of the poet shaken by a year of defeat, asking whether he must now chant cold dirges and hymns of defeat; war, grief and the poet's vocation.

title: Years of the Modern
author: Whitman
cluster: Money and Gold · Marriage and Fidelity · Social Injustice
summary: A visionary free-verse prophecy of a coming democratic world-era, solidarity of races and falling thrones, staged as theatrum mundi; themes of democracy and the new era.

title: Yet, Yet, Ye Downcast Hours
author: Whitman
summary: Poem of dark downcast hours and the dread that matter is conqueror; the dying voices cry out for their destination as the speaker prepares to sail.

title: Yonnondio
author: Whitman
summary: A dirge for vanished Native American races who pass like ghosts and disappear unrecorded, a lament of transience.

title: You Felons on Trial in Courts
author: Whitman
summary: Confessional identification of the poet with felons, convicts, and prostitutes, refusing to deny the lusts and wickedness in himself; the outcast, guilt, the body, and social compassion.

title: You Lingering Sparse Leaves of Me
author: Whitman
summary: The poet likens himself to a well-shorn tree's last sparse leaves on winter-nearing boughs, the hardiest and last.

title: You Say You Love
author: Keats
summary: A refrain-song reproaching a cold, nun-like beloved whose professions of love lack warmth; plea for true passion against a statue-like reserve.

title: YOUTH AND AGE
author: Coleridge
summary: A lyric on the passage from youth to age, Youth imagined as a bold masker now departed, with the body a 'breathing house' grown burdensome. Themes: transience, ageing, nostalgia, melancholy.

title: Youth, Day, Old Age and Night
author: Whitman
summary: A short free-verse epigram pairing youth/age and day/night, affirming that old age and the restoring night follow with equal grace.

title: ZAPOLYA A CHRISTMAS TALE IN TWO PARTS
author: Coleridge
cluster: Power and Corruption · The Crown · Pride
summary: Coleridge's romance verse-drama in blank verse, modelled on Shakespeare's Winter's Tale: a usurper (Emerick) seizes the throne of Illyria, the rightful queen and infant heir are driven into exile, and after twenty years legitimacy is restored. Central themes are kingship and legitimacy, usurpation, fate and providence, exile, and the restoration of the natural order.
